claims.statement: Phi_t is balanced. Its Walsh coefficient W(a) = sum_x (-1)^(Phi_t(x) xor a.x) is 0 whenever a_{-t} = 0, so Phi_t is uncorrelated with every affine function not involving x_{-t}. W(e_{-t}) = 2 sum_{x'} (-1)^Psi_t(x'). Numerically W(e_{-t})/2^{2t+1} is nonzero for 2 <= t <= 11, so Phi_t is not 1-resilient there.
claims.proof: If a_{-t} = 0, then Phi_t xor a.x = x_{-t} xor (a function of the other variables), which is balanced, so W(a) = 0. If a = e_{-t}, then Phi_t xor x_{-t} = Psi_t, which does not depend on x_{-t}, giving the factor 2. Balance of Phi_t is the a = 0 case. The numerical values (anf2.c, full Walsh transform) are W(e_{-t})/2^{2t+1} = 0.25, -0.25, 0.156, -0.078, 0.075, -0.069, 0.076, -0.050, 0.021, -0.021 for t = 2..11, with sign (-1)^t. Overall max|W|/2^{2t+1} = 0.047 at t = 11. These are statements about Phi_t on general inputs and do not constrain the single-seed orbit.
claims.evidence: anf.c and anf2.c truth-table Walsh transforms for t <= 11.

claims.statement: Barrier. Rules 90 (l xor r), 150 (l xor c xor r) and 210 (l xor (not c and r)) have the same form as rule 30, l xor g(c,r) with g(0,0) = 0. So they are left-permutive with a two-sided single-seed light cone, Jen's adjacent/strip argument applies to them verbatim, and their right diagonals are 2-power periodic with the odometer structure of claims A and B. Yet their single-seed center columns are eventually periodic: rules 90 and 210 give 1,0,0,..., and rule 150 gives all 1 (rule 210's single-seed pattern equals rule 90's). Among the 8 ECAs l xor g(c,r) with g(0,0) = 0 (240, 60, 90, 150, 120, 30, 180, 210), rule 30 is the only one whose center is not eventually periodic within 1200 steps. High algebraic degree does not help either: all 34 ECAs with maximal degree deg Phi_7 = 15 = 2t+1 have eventually periodic single-seed centers (e.g. rule 254 = l or c or r: degree 2t+1, center all 1), as do 113 of the 128 ECAs with deg Phi_7 >= 12. Conclusion: a proof of Problem 1 must use a property specific to g = c or r. Left-permutivity, the edges, Jen's theorem, 2-adic diagonal structure and ANF degree are jointly insufficient.
claims.proof: Rule 90: two steps give cell(t+2,p) = cell(t,p-2) xor cell(t,p+2), the Frobenius identity (z+1/z)^2 = z^2 + z^-2. By induction, cell(t,p) = 0 when t+p is odd, and cell(2t,2p) = cell(t,p). For t >= 1: odd t gives center 0 by parity; t = 2s gives center(2s) = center(s), and strong induction finishes. Rule 150: two steps give cell(t+2,p) = cell(t,p-2) xor cell(t,p) xor cell(t,p+2). By induction, cell(2t,2p) = cell(t,p) and cell(2t,2p+1) = 0. Then center(2s) = center(s) and center(2s+1) = cell(2s,-1) xor cell(2s,0) xor cell(2s,1) = center(s), so the center is 1 everywhere (the central trinomial coefficients are odd). Rule 210 differs from rule 90 only when c = r = 1, and that never happens on rule 90's checkerboard support (adjacent cells have opposite t+p parity). So the two patterns coincide by induction. Kernel-checked as center90, center150, cell210_eq_cell90 and center210 in /Users/swish/.claude/jobs/b8cd2926/tmp/r30prize/gf2-algebra/lean/LeftPermutiveBarrier.lean (no sorry). Jen's argument applies to these rules because it uses only cell(t,i-1) = cell(t+1,i) xor g(cell(t,i), cell(t,i+1)) and the left edge cell(t,-t) = 1 with zeros beyond, which hold whenever g(0,1) = 1. Claims A and B use only the form l xor g(c,r) with g(0,0) = 0. Rule 254's Phi_t is the OR of 2t+1 variables, which has degree 2t+1. The degree counts come from scan256.py and scan256b.py (big-int truth tables plus a center-column periodicity test over 2000 steps).

claims.statement: Let cellW be rule 30 started from all black except a white cell at 0. Then cellW(t+1, p) = cell(t, p-1), so the white-seed center column is (0, cell(0,-1), cell(1,-1), ...), i.e. column -1 of the usual pattern delayed one step. Hence, by Jen's theorem, rule 30's center column is not eventually periodic from a single black cell, or from a single white cell on a black background, or both. Equivalently, rule 135 (not l xor (c and r)), the black-white conjugate of rule 30, satisfies cell135(t+1, 0) = not cell(t,-1) from one black cell, so Problem 1 holds for rule 30 or for rule 135. Rule 149 has the same center as 135 and rule 86 the same as 30, by mirror symmetry.
claims.proof: For t = 0: in the white-seed row, positions -1, 0, 1 see the neighborhoods 110, 101, 011, and rule 30 maps these to 0, 0, 1. Every other position sees 111, which maps to 0. So F30(white seed) = e_1, a single black cell at 1. Induction on t then gives cellW(t+1,p) = cell(t,p-1). If the white-seed center were periodic from T with period P, then column -1 would be periodic from T: cell(t+P,-1) = cellW(t+P+1,0) = cellW(t+1,0) = cell(t,-1). If the black-seed center were also eventually periodic, Jen's theorem (Rule30Jen.jen 0 (-1)) gives a contradiction. For rule 135: F135 = not . F30 . not, so the pattern from e_0 is not of the F30 pattern from the white seed, giving cell135(t+1,p) = not cell(t,p-1). Kernel-checked as cellW_succ, problem1_black_or_white, cell135_succ and problem1_30_or_135 in /Users/swish/.claude/jobs/b8cd2926/tmp/r30prize/gf2-algebra/lean/Rule135Center.lean (imports Rule30Jen; no sorry). This is an immediate corollary of Jen and may be folklore; I have not seen it stated.
claims.evidence: Checked numerically for t < 400. Lean #eval of the rule 135 center: 1,1,0,0,1,1,0,1,0, which equals not col_{-1} shifted by one step.

claims.statement: This is a local fact about any rule-30 space-time pattern, with any initial condition. If the center column satisfies c(tau) = 1 for tau = t-1 (mod 2) and c(tau) = 0 for tau = t (mod 2), for all tau in [t-1, t+4], i.e. it reads 101010 there, then cell(t,-4) = 0. Under the same hypothesis, column 1 satisfies cell(t,1) and cell(t+2,1) = 0. Corollary: if the single-seed center were eventually 2-periodic and not constant, column -4 would be eventually white on one parity class of times. So excluding least period 2 for every transient reduces to proving that column -4 is black infinitely often at even times and infinitely often at odd times.
claims.proof:
Write t = 2s+1, x(i) = cell(i,1) and Lk(i) = cell(i,-k), so c(2s..2s+5) = 1,0,1,0,1,0. The steps below use only the rule at the indicated cells.
(1) Center rule c(i+1) = L1(i) xor (c(i) or x(i)): at i = 2s+1, 2s+2, 2s+3, 2s+4 it gives L1(2s+1) = not b, L1(2s+2) = 1, L1(2s+3) = not b', L1(2s+4) = 1, where b = x(2s+1) and b' = x(2s+3).
(2) Column-1 rule x(i+1) = c(i) xor (x(i) or cell(i,2)): at i = 2s+1, x(2s+2) >= x(2s+1); at i = 2s+2, x(2s+3) <= not x(2s+2). So b and b' = 0 (OR monotonicity and blocking).
(3) Rule at column -1, L1(i+1) = L2(i) xor (L1(i) or c(i)): at i = 2s+1, 2s+2, 2s+3 it gives L2(2s+1) = b, L2(2s+2) = b', L2(2s+3) = b'.
(4) Rule at column -2, L2(i+1) = L3(i) xor (L2(i) or L1(i)): at i = 2s+1 it gives L3(2s+1) = not b'; at i = 2s+2 it gives L3(2s+2) = not b'.
(5) Rule at column -3, L3(i+1) = L4(i) xor (L3(i) or L2(i)), at i = 2s+1: L4(2s+1) = not b' xor (not b' or b) = b and b' = 0.
The corollary: an eventually 2-periodic center with least period 2 alternates, and every late time t with c(t-1) = 1 satisfies the hypothesis. Verified exhaustively (p2check.c, p2win.c) over all rule-30 patches on columns [-6,3] with free boundary columns: when the center is constrained to 101010 on times 0..5 only, cell(1,-4) = 0 in all 65536 such patches.
claims.evidence: In the true pattern, column -4 has 24957 black cells at even times (last at t = 99998) and 24865 at odd times (last at t = 99995) for t < 10^5, so the lemma excludes period 2 only within computed ranges. The OR-free exploration p2left.py (random golden-mean column 1, 60 columns) shows this is the only forced parity class beyond column -1, so the reduction does not propagate further by local means.

claims.statement: Relation to linear rules. All 8 quiescent additive ECAs have eventually constant single-seed centers: rules 60, 102, 150 and 204 give all 1; rules 90, 170 and 240 give 1,0,0,...; rule 0 gives 1,0,.... So the premise that these linear rules have nontrivial 2-automatic centers is false; only their off-center columns are nontrivial (e.g. rule 90 column 2 is black exactly at t = 2^{k+1} - 2). Exact bridge: rule 30 = rule 150 xor (c and r) gives c(t) = 1 xor XOR_{s<t} XOR_p Tri(t-1-s, p) cell(s,p) cell(s,p+1), where Tri(n,p) = [z^p](z^-1 + 1 + z)^n mod 2. Using rule 240 (shift) as the linear part instead gives the brief's parity identity.
claims.proof: Rules 60 and 102: cell(t,p) = binomial(t, +-p) mod 2, and the center binomial(t,0) = 1. Rule 90: the center is binomial(t,t/2) for even t, and binomial(2k,k) = 2 binomial(2k-1,k-1) is even for k >= 1. Rule 150: the center is the central trinomial coefficient sum_k binomial(t,2k) binomial(2k,k), which is 1 mod 2. Rules 170 and 240 are shifts; 204 is the identity; 0 is null. (Rules 90 and 150 are kernel-checked in LeftPermutiveBarrier.lean.) Rule 90 column 2: binomial(2s, s+1) is odd iff (s-1) + (s+1) has no binary carries, iff s = 2^k - 1. Duhamel: with X_t(z) = sum_p cell(t,p) z^p, X_{t+1} = (z + 1 + 1/z) X_t + N(X_t), where N(X)_p = X_p X_{p+1}. Iterating, X_t = L^t X_0 + sum_{s<t} L^{t-1-s} N(X_s). Take the z^0 coefficient and use [z^0] L^t e_0 = 1.

claims.statement: Linear complexity over GF(2) is a complete invariant: c is eventually periodic iff L(c[0..n)) is bounded, and transient T with period P forces L(c[0..n)) <= T+P for all n. Berlekamp-Massey gives L(c[0..10^6)) = 499,998 and |L(c[0..n)) - n/2| <= 9.5 for all n <= 10^6 (maximum at n = 937,375). Columns -1 and +1 behave the same way (max deviations 8.5 and 9.0 for n <= 199,000). Consequence: any eventual period satisfies T + P >= 499,998. This is weaker than the existing 10^9-bit window data, but uniform in how T+P splits.
claims.proof: If c(t+P) = c(t) for all t >= T, then c(n) = c(n-P) for all n >= T+P. That is a linear feedback shift register of length T+P with connection polynomial 1 + D^P, so every prefix has linear complexity <= T+P. Conversely, bounded linear complexity means a single linear recurrence over the finite field GF(2) generates c, so c is eventually periodic. The numbers come from bm2.c (bit-packed BM on center-1e7.bin), cross-checked against the plain implementation bm_ref.py up to n = 3000. Columns ±1 come from r30cols.c, with column 0 matched bit-for-bit against the stored center data. The profile matches the random-sequence behavior n/2 + O(log n).

claims.statement: Conjecture (generalized Problem 1): for every finite nonzero initial configuration, no column of rule 30 is eventually periodic. Jen's argument already gives at most one periodic column per seed.
claims.proof: Not proved. Evidence (seeds.c): for every seed of width <= 14 (8192 odd seeds), every column in [-30, 44], and every period P <= 400 tested on t in [1500, 3000), no column is periodic. The first version of the program had a stale-buffer bug that produced false positives; it was fixed and rerun. Why it matters: since no finite seed shows a periodic column, an argument that never uses the specific seed is not refuted by this test. Claim F shows that such an argument must still use the OR.

claims.statement: Experiment, with a conjecture on period 4. A center word w absorbs if the right half driven by w^inf from any finite state has eventually periodic column 1; by Jen this excludes w for every transient. From random finite right-half states (absorbP.c; 5 to 40 trials, up to 20000 steps, period test <= 1024 with >= 3000 comparisons), the number of primitive words, up to rotation, absorbed in every trial is: P=2: 0/1, P=3: 0/2, P=4: 3/3 (0001 and 0011 give column-1 period 4, 0111 gives period 8; 40/40 trials), P=5: 0/6, P=6: 0/9, P=7: 0/18, P=8: 7/30, P=9: 0/56, P=10: 17/99, P=11: 38/186, P=12: 46/335. Conjecture: all three primitive period-4 words absorb from every finite state, which would exclude least period 4 for all transients. Absorption on the left side is impossible by Jen, since the left half is permutive from the edge.
claims.proof: Not proved. The local-trap test (trap.py) finds, for 0001, 0011 and 0111 with m <= 12 right columns and an adversarial column m+1, a single terminal SCC in which column 1 is not periodic. So absorption is not caused by a local barrier that holds against arbitrary far-right behavior. A proof must use the actual dynamics of the far right half. Important negative consequence: no word of period 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 or 9 absorbs, so the absorbing-word route cannot exclude those periods at all.

claims.statement: Refuted approach: purely local constraints do not exclude small periods. Hypothesis tested: c = w^inf from some T, together with the exact rule on right columns 1..m-1, the constraint x_m(t) = 1 => x_m(t+1) = not x_{m-1}(t) on the last column, and leftward reconstruction of columns -1..-m, forces some neighboring column to be eventually periodic (which Jen would forbid). Exhaustive automaton computation (forcing.py: SCC and phase-consistency test on a state space of size 2^m P) shows this happens only for P = 1 (w = 0 and w = 1, reproducing the known constant-column argument). It never happens for any primitive word of period 2 to 5 with m <= 9.
claims.proof: The automaton encodes only necessary conditions, so if forcing occurred it would give a rigorous transient-independent exclusion. It does not: every nontrivial SCC that could force a column contains branching paths whose column labels are not periodic. For P = 2 the only forced facts are column -1 = 1 at the center's 1-phase and the column -4 parity class (claim H). The underlying reason is that the left half is locally free (left-permutivity), and the last right column is free whenever it is white.

claims.statement: Generating-function and automaticity tests (evidence only). The 2-kernel of c shows no finiteness: all 2^{K+1}-1 sequences c(2^k n + r) (k <= K, r < 2^k) are pairwise distinct on n < 64 for K <= 13. The GF(2) binomial (Mahler) transform of c on [0, 2^17) has density 0.499 of ones, and about 0.5 within every popcount class. Algebraic identity: with omega a primitive cube root of unity in GF(4), z + 1 + 1/z vanishes at omega, so X_{t+1}(omega) = sum_p cell(t,p) cell(t,p+1) omega^p. This gives no handle on the center.
claims.proof: The identity is X_{t+1} = (z+1+1/z) X_t + N(X_t) evaluated at omega, where 1 + omega + omega^2 = 0. kernel.py and the inline transform script produced the counts. Eventually periodic sequences are k-automatic for every k, so a finite 2-kernel would be necessary for periodicity; the observed growth is evidence, not proof.

result.failed_approaches:
1. Linear complexity / rationality of C(x) = sum c(t) x^t. Over GF(2), "eventually periodic" is the same as "rational" and the same as "bounded linear complexity", so this is a reformulation, not an invariant. Berlekamp-Massey shows L(n) = n/2 + O(10) up to 10^6, which gives only T+P >= 499,998.

2. Furstenberg/Christol diagonal approach. c is the main diagonal of the array Q(i,j) = cell((i+j)/2, (i-j)/2), whose columns are purely 2-power periodic and whose rows are eventually periodic with tiny periods. No algebraicity of the bivariate series is available, and c sits in the transient part of every row and the first period of every column. The 2-kernel test shows no automaticity.

3. 2-adic/Mahler/odometer structure of the diagonals (claims A-C). It is rigorous but controls only a band of about 2.3*log2(t) diagonals near the right edge (and transients near the left edge). Rules 90, 150 and 210 share all of it while having periodic centers (claim F), so it cannot decide Problem 1.

4. ANF degree and correlation immunity of Phi_t (claims D, E). Exact degree 2t-1 is proven, but these properties concern general inputs. All 34 maximal-degree ECAs have periodic single-seed centers, so degree carries no information about the single orbit.

5. Local algebraic forcing (claim M). Automata with <= 9 right columns plus leftward reconstruction plus Jen exclude no word of period 2 to 5. For period 2 the only consequence is column -4 vanishing on one parity class (claim H). Feeding the golden-mean column-1 constraint into the rotated (leftward) dynamics forces nothing beyond column -4 (p2left.py, 60 columns).

6. Local traps for absorbing words (claim L). For the period-4 words that absorb empirically, there is no terminal SCC with periodic column 1 when column m+1 is adversarial (m <= 12). The absorption must therefore come from global right-half dynamics.

7. Absorbing words for periods 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9. No word of these periods absorbs, so this route cannot reach them. Left absorption is impossible by Jen.

8. The arXiv 2604.00165 framework (rule 22 as a symmetric reference). It has no periodicity result; its rule-30 statements are empirical or formal.

9. Counting/overdetermination heuristic. A periodic c leaves about T free bits in the left half against about N/2 parity constraints, so it is overdetermined for N >> T. But the constraints become independent only once the left edge's influence arrives (t > 2T), and nothing makes this uniform in T.
result.most_promising_next_step:
By claim F, any proof must exploit OR-specific monotonicity and blocking, so I see two concrete targets.

(a) Least period 4 for all transients. Prove that each of the three primitive period-4 center words (0001, 0011, 0111) absorbs: the rule-30 right half driven by w^inf from any finite configuration has eventually periodic column 1. Empirically it absorbs in 40 of 40 random trials, with column-1 period 4 or 8. Combined with Jen and the proven constant case, this would exclude every eventual period whose least period is 4. Claim L shows the proof cannot be a local-barrier argument (no trap with <= 12 columns against an adversarial right side). It must track how the chaotic far-right region's leftward influence is blocked by the OR. Natural tools are the per-block normal form of column 1 forced by OR-monotonicity during zero-runs of c (column 1 = 0^a 1^b on each zero-run), and a potential function on the boundary layer.

(b) Period 2 cannot be reached by absorption. Claim H reduces "no eventual period 2" to showing that column -4 of the single-seed pattern is black infinitely often at both even and odd times. This could be attacked with the same OR-monotonicity used for "no column eventually constant": assume column q is eventually white on a parity class, derive monotonicity of a neighboring column on alternate steps, and try to reach two adjacent eventually periodic columns.

result.gaps:
None of these gaps is fatal. Items 1–3 are routine steps the proof states without proof. I filled each one in and it holds. Item 4 is a wording issue. Item 5 is a factual error, but it sits in the evidence, not in the claim.
1. (v), finite X_f ⇒ eventually periodic. The proof says the words occurring infinitely often number at most K for each length. That needs the compactness (König) extension lemma, which the proof does not state: every word u occurring infinitely often in f equals x[0,|u|) for some x in X_f. Proof of the lemma: some pair (a,b) surrounds infinitely many occurrences, so aub also occurs infinitely often. Repeat this and take the limit; then use shift-invariance of X_f.
2. (v), eventually periodic ⇒ |X_f| = P. The proof says X_f is the orbit of the periodic tail but never shows X_f contains nothing more. Fill-in: let y = ...vvv... (two-sided). Every factor of y of length P+1 satisfies w[i+P] = w[i], so every x in X_f has period P. Then x[0,P) is a rotation of v, so x = σ^s y. The P shifts are distinct: σ^s y = y with 0 < s < P would give y the period gcd(s,P) < P (Bezout works on Z), and then the tail f[T,∞) would have that period too, contradicting minimality. The minimal eventual period does not depend on T, because any eventual period of a sequence that is P-periodic from T holds from T itself.
3. (vi), (i) ⇒ (vi). The step "a rotation equal to itself forces j ≡ T (mod P) by minimality" is the same gcd/primitive-word argument as in item 2. It is correct but terse.
4. Wording in the 'Consequently' part. "No factor has eventually constant return words" must be read as "no factor occurring infinitely often", as (vi) itself states. Whether c has factors that occur only finitely often is unknown. If such a factor occurs at least twice, its return-word sequence is finite and could be called trivially eventually constant, which would make the literal statement wrong. With the qualifier it is correct.

**Expansion and linear complexity.**
- By Lucas, binom(t,m) mod 2 = [bits(m) contained in bits(t)]. So for m < 2^e it depends only on t mod 2^e, and these functions are unitriangular in subset order. Mobius inversion therefore gives the unique expansion with mu_m = sum over k contained in m of u(k).
- Pascal mod 2 gives Delta binom(.,m) = binom(.,m-1). Since x^{2^e}+1 = (x+1)^{2^e}, the minimal polynomial is (x+1)^L with L = 1 + top index.
- u is 2^f-periodic exactly when top index < 2^f. So the least period, which divides 2^e, is 2^{ceil(log2 L)}.
- Hockey stick: sum_{s<t} binom(s,m) = binom(t,m+1), so S raises every index by 1.

**(a)** R_j(0) = 0 for j >= 1, so R_j = S(R_{j-1} or R_{j-2}). The input is nonzero, so L_j = L(input) + 1.

**(b)**
- Upper bound: the OR has period 2^max, and S at most doubles the period.
- Lower bound: R_j(t) = cell(t, t-j) = 0 for t < j/2, by the light cone. R_j(ceil(j/2)) = 1: for even j this is the left edge; for odd j it is D_1, which equals 1 for t >= 1 since cell(t+1,-t) = 0 xor (1 or .) = 1.
- If L_j <= ceil(j/2), the first L_j values are all zero, so (1+E)^{L_j} R_j = 0 forces R_j = 0, a contradiction. Hence L_j >= ceil(j/2) + 1 and 2^{e_j} >= ceil(j/2) + 1.

**(c)** The input is 2^{e_j-1}-periodic, so L(input) <= 2^{e_j-1}. Least period 2^{e_j} forces L_j > 2^{e_j-1}, so L_j = 2^{e_j-1} + 1.

**(d)**
- Write M = 2^{e_j-1}. R_j has top index exactly M. m* = L_{j-1} - 1 < M because e_{j-1} <= e_j - 1.
- The product terms binom(t,M)*binom(t,m2) give index M | m2 = M + m2, each exactly once. Products of indices below M stay below M.
- So the top index of the OR is M + m*, with coefficient 1. This needs m* >= 1: if m* = 0 then R_{j-1} = 1 and the OR collapses to the constant 1, so the hypothesis L_{j-1} >= 2 is necessary.

result.summary:
No small period (2, 3 or 4) could be excluded for all transients. What was achieved, with honest status:

PROVED AND CHECKED IN LEAN (scratch files, standard axioms only, no sorry, no native_decide):
(1) Effective boundary lemma: for every t, cell(t,-1) || c(t) = cell(t,-1) || (c(t) && c(t+1)). So the left half evolves exactly as if column 0 held c'(t) = c(t) and c(t+1). If the period word has no two cyclically adjacent 1s (01, 001, 0001, ...), the left half from T on is an autonomous system: rule 30 on p <= -1 with a white column 0, which I call the zero-boundary left half (ZBL).
(2) 9-step absorption: nine consecutive black center cells force (cell 1, cell 2) = (0,1), and that pair persists while the center stays black. 9 is the smallest number of steps that works.
(3) Long-ones theorem: for EVERY transient T, the center column is not eventually periodic with any period word whose cyclic runs of 1s all have length >= 9 (e.g. 0^k 1^m with m >= 9). The proof forces column 1 at every white center cell, which makes column -1 eventually periodic; Jen's theorem then gives the contradiction.
(4) Period-2 rigidity facts: under an alternating center, column -1 is black at every c=1 time and column -4 is white at every c=0 time. Column 1, read in pairs aligned with the c=0 times, never shows 00 00, 01 01 or 00 01 00 01. Consequently the zeros of column -1 are 4 to 10 steps apart.

COMPUTER-ASSISTED, NOT YET IN LEAN (two independent implementations, C and Python, agree): adversarial-strip certificates exclude 18 specific words of periods 8, 10, 11 and 12 for every T (e.g. 00000011 and 01111111). No word of length 2 to 7 or 9, other than "1", has such a certificate at strip widths up to 14 to 18.

REDUCTIONS AND OBSTRUCTIONS:
- Period 2 follows from a clean statement about the autonomous ZBL: no finite left configuration makes column -1 black at every other step forever. Exhaustive search supports it (survival at most about 2W steps for width W <= 24), but it is unproved. Finiteness is essential: the infinite stripe configuration ...10101 satisfies the constraint forever.
- The period-4 words 0001, 0011 and 0111 have verified forward-invariant traps (sets of strip states closed under any input from the right) in which column 1 is periodic. Entering a trap would give a contradiction via Jen. Whether the trap is always reached is open and cannot be certified by any bounded-width adversarial strip: the number of avoiding states grows about 1.87^W.
- No argument confined to a bounded space-time window or to a two-sided strip can exclude any period, so a proof must use an edge of the light cone.

claims.statement: Effective boundary. For every t >= 0: cell(t,-1) || c(t) = cell(t,-1) || (c(t) && c(t+1)), where c(t) = cell(t,0). Hence the left half {p <= -1} evolves exactly as rule 30 on the half-line driven at column 0 by c'(t) := c(t) && c(t+1). Corollaries: (i) c(t)=1 implies cell(t,-1) = not c(t+1). (ii) Suppose c is eventually periodic from T with a period word w that has no two cyclically adjacent 1s (01, 001, 0001, 00101, ...). Then for t >= T the left half is the AUTONOMOUS zero-boundary left half (ZBL: rule 30 on p <= -1 with column 0 replaced by 0), started from the finite configuration cell(T, p<0), and cell(t,-1) = 1 at every t >= T with c(t) = 1.

The left side is then 1, and the right side is (not c(t+1)) || c(t+1) = 1. Column 0 enters the evolution of the cells p <= -1 only through cell(t+1,-1) = cell(t,-2) xor (cell(t,-1) || c(t)). claims.statement: Long-ones theorem (every transient). Let T >= 0 and P > 0 with c(t+P) = c(t) for all t >= T. Then it is impossible that every 1->0 transition of c at a time t >= T+9 is preceded by at least 9 ones (c(t-9..t-1) = 1). Equivalently: the center column is not eventually periodic with any period word whose cyclic maximal runs of 1s all have length >= 9, for any transient and any phase. Examples: 0^k 1^m with m >= 9, 01^9 01^12, 0^5 1^10 0 1^9.
claims.proof: Case 1: c has no 1 in [T, T+P). Then c is eventually 0, contradicting no_column_eventually_constant. Case 2: there is a 1 at some u in [T, T+P). By periodicity every window [s, s+P) with s >= T contains a 1. Fix t >= T+9+P with c(t) = 0 and let s be the first 0 of the 0-run containing t. The window [t-P, t-1] contains a 1, so s >= t-P+1 > T+9, and c(s-1) = 1. By hypothesis c(s-9..s-1) = 1, so C2 gives (cell(s,1), cell(s,2)) = (0,1). Inside the 0-run, cell(j+1,1) = 0 xor (cell(j,1) || cell(j,2)) = 1 for j = s, s+1, ..., t-1: at j=s because cell(s,2)=1, later because cell(j,1)=1. So cell(t,1) = 0 when t = s (then c(t-1)=1) and cell(t,1) = 1 when t > s (then c(t-1)=0). In both cases cell(t,1) = not c(t-1). By cell_left at 0, for t >= T+P+10, cell(t,-1) = c(t+1) xor (c(t) || cell(t,1)) = c(t+1) xor (c(t) || not c(t-1)) (if c(t)=1 the cell(t,1) term is irrelevant). This is P-periodic. So columns -1 and 0 are both eventually periodic, contradicting Jen's not_adjacent (-1).

result.failed_approaches:
1. Absorbing words via the right half alone (the brief's idea), refined. It suffices that column 1 is eventually periodic at the zero-phases of w, because column -1 reads b only there. This works with bounded transients only for words with long runs (C3, C4). It fails for every word of length 2..7. For 01 and 011, column 1 under the periodic driver is numerically aperiodic: for 01 it is a positive-entropy concatenation of 110100 and 1101000100. For 001 it is sometimes trapped (column-1 period 21) and sometimes not. For 0001, 0011 and 0111 the trap is always reached in experiments, but transients are unbounded in practice (522 found). An adversary at any strip width can avoid the trap (C9), so no finite-state certificate exists.

2. Left-only constraint plus edge (left-permutive extension and the zero region). With c periodic and column -1 forced at the phases where c=1, the extension's time-T row cells x_{-n}(T) are Boolean functions of all earlier free bits. Their degree grows with n, the even cells depend on all previous odd cells, and there is no bounded-memory recurrence or linear (GF(2)) invariant. The finiteness condition is an overdetermined infinite system that empirically fails within about 2W steps but resists proof. Forced-cell analysis finds only column -1 at odd phases and column -4 at even phases forced for period 2 (columns -1..-4 and -8 partially for 001); no whole column becomes periodic, so Jen cannot be applied.

3. Time-shift difference D = X_t xor X_{t+P}. The rightmost left difference moves right at speed >= 1 and must be absorbed at column 0 exactly when D_t(1) = 1 and c(t) = 0. This gives a correct coupling, but no contradiction, since everything is locally consistent (C10).

4. Diagonal-period arguments. Right diagonals born under a periodic driver still have huge periods (none within 4000 steps), so no collapse of e_j occurs. Left-diagonal settling under periodic or zero boundaries still leaves a chaotic region about t/4 wide next to column 0. No 2-adic conflict with odd periods was found.

5. Kolmogorov/information counting fails, because the true configuration is computable from T.

6. Global strip abstractions: two-sided strips always admit periodic c (C10); right strips with larger W only shrink the trap-avoiding fraction geometrically (about 0.935^W), never to 0.

7. The empirical eventual constraint 'CA forbidden' turned out false (C11).
result.most_promising_next_step:
Attack the clean autonomous statement Q_01 (C6/C7). Show that rule 30 on the half-line p <= -1, with column 0 forced white and started from any finite configuration, cannot keep cell(t,-1) = 1 at every other time step forever. If needed, add the rigorously available side constraint that the zeros of column -1 are 4-10 steps apart (C5e). This alone would exclude period 2 for all transients. It must use finiteness, since the stripe configuration is a counterexample among infinite configurations. A plausible route is backward determinism under the constraint: at the forced steps, the configuration at t determines the one at t-1. Combine it with the eventually periodic left-edge diagonals to show that the constraint, propagated along right diagonals to the edge region, contradicts their power-of-2 periodicity.

In parallel, prove that the traps for 0001, 0011 and 0111 are always reached (C9), which would cut period 4 down to period 2. This cannot be done with any finite strip and needs global information about the right half.

Cheap wins: move LongOnes.lean and PeriodTwo.lean into Ruliology (they compile against Rule30Prize as is). Implement the kernel-checked bitset certificate (C4 lean_plan) and run the certificate search over longer words, to grow the list of words excluded for every transient.

result.counterexample_or_check:
I found no counterexample. Every step is backed by a separate check:
(1) C2, the absorption lemma: if c(s-9..s-1)=1 then (cell(s,1),cell(s,2))=(0,1). I wrote new code for this in /Users/swish/.claude/jobs/b8cd2926/tmp/r30prize/verify-C3-longones/absorb_indep.py. It shares nothing with the agent's Lean helpers. It runs all 2^11 states of columns 1..11 with the center held at 1 for 9 steps, and gets 0 failures. Padding the state with random bits past column 11 never changes the result, which confirms the dependence on columns 1..11 only. It also shows 9 is the smallest count that works: after 8 ones, (1,0) can still occur.
(2) On the real rule 30 pattern for t < 6000 (real_check.py), three things held everywhere they apply: absorption (7 windows), cell_left at column 0 (every t), and the key identity cell(t,1) = not c(t-1) for white cells whose white run follows ≥9 ones (16 cells).
(3) Lean: `timeout 60 lake env lean .../smallperiods/lean/LongOnes.lean` from ruliology-lean exits 0 with no errors or warnings in about 5 s. `no_period_long_ones` uses only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. `absorb` uses only [propext, Quot.sound], so `decide +kernel` was used, not `native_decide` (no `ofReduceBool`). There is no sorry, axiom, implemented_by, extern or unsafe in LongOnes.lean, Rule30Prize.lean or Rule30Jen.lean. The Rule30Prize and Rule30Jen .olean files are newer than their sources. The Lean hypotheses say exactly what the claim says. Natural-number subtraction in `center (t-1-i)` is exact because t ≥ T+9 ≥ 9 and i < 9.
result.gaps:
I found no essential gaps. Minor points:
(a) The 'Equivalently' version (cyclic 1-runs of the period word all ≥ 9, any transient, any phase) is not in Lean. I checked by hand that it follows from the formal version both ways. Cyclic runs ≥ 9 implies the hypothesis: for t ≥ T+9 the 9 cells before t lie in the periodic part. An all-ones word makes the hypothesis vacuous and is excluded by center_not_eventually_constant. In the other direction, take a late copy of any run.
(b) The proof relies on rule30Jen.not_adjacent and center_not_eventually_constant. I read both proofs in ruliology-lean: periodic_left_all plus the left edge, and the mono/const argument. They are sound and kernel-checked.
(c) Scope: this excludes only period words whose 1-runs all have length ≥ 9. The absorption lemma needs exactly 9 ones for an arbitrary right-half state, so the method does not reach shorter runs without more information about the actual right half.
result.verdict_summary:

RIGOROUS RESULTS (Lean)
- Masked Jen: column i cannot be eventually periodic while column i+1, restricted to the zeros of column i, is also eventually periodic with a common period. This is the sharp "absorption" criterion. For example, it makes 0111 absorbing, which corrects the round-1 note.
- Black-run lemma: 9 consecutive black center cells force column 1 white and column 2 black. Consequence: no eventually periodic center column whose repeating block has all black runs of length at least 9. This includes (0 1^k)^∞ for every k ≥ 9, for any transient. The smallperiods agent found the same lemma independently.
- A general strip-certificate method with a Lean soundness theorem (`Cert.sound`). It combines a rank function and a position labelling on the finite graph of the right strip (rule 30 at columns 1..b, column b+1 unknown) with masked Jen. Kernel-checked exclusions, for every transient, of tails with these repeating blocks: 01111111, 00000011, 0^10 1, 000000000101 and 0011111111. None of these is covered by the black-run theorem.
- Period-2 rigid structure: an alternating tail forces column -1 to be black at the black times, the golden-mean constraint on column -1 at the white times, and column -4 white at every white time.

CRITICAL FINDINGS (exhaustive computation)
- Local arguments provably cannot handle short periods. For every primitive period word of length 2 to 7, at every strip width up to 16 (up to 20 for 0001), the strip relaxation admits histories in which column 1 on the white times is aperiodic. Adding Jen-type constraints does not remove them.
- All 183 certified words contain a run of at least 6 equal symbols. The certified fraction is 2–3% for periods 12 to 16.
- How long a nonzero finite configuration of radius r can fake a periodic center column behaves like a random-constraint model for periods 2 to 4 (about 1.25r to 1.9r). For period 1 it is exactly r+2, matching Condrey's 2026 constant-trace paper. So an exact classification like Condrey's is unlikely for P ≥ 2.
- The map from a finite configuration to its center column is not injective: δ0 and δ0+δ1 have the same center column (proved by hand).
- The left half has no local constraints, and its driver-influence spreads at about 0.24t even for periodic drivers.
- Absorption is non-local. It happens from 100% of more than 4000 finitely supported right halves for all period-4 words, with absorption time independent of width. Certified traps exist (109/188/188 states). But no finite strip forces entry into them.

THREE RESEARCH PROGRAMS
- (A) Local forcing certificates plus masked Jen. This already gives infinitely many excluded periodic patterns. Next steps: uniform families via a pumping lemma, and a precise characterization of which words are certifiable. It provably cannot reach periods 2 to 7.
- (B) Non-local absorption for powers-of-two periods, starting with period 4. The conjecture is that every finitely supported right half driven by a period-4 word absorbs. Proving it would rule out least period 4 for all transients. A proof must use finite support or the right edge, because finite strips are not enough.
- (C) Global two-sided matching, the uniform periodic-trace conjecture (UPTC). Given any right half and target trace there is at most one compatible left half. Problem 1 follows if no nonzero finite configuration has a purely periodic trace. The remaining obstruction is finiteness of the left reconstruction from (c, σc⊕(c∨col1)). Faking-horizon data show this needs a genuinely global invariant linking the left edge's zero-wedge to the driven right half.

No claim here proves Problem 1, and no full period has been excluded beyond period 1.

claims.statement: Masked Jen. For every column i of the single-seed rule-30 pattern there are no T and Q>0 such that cell(t+Q,i)=cell(t,i) for all t>=T and cell(t+Q,i+1)=cell(t,i+1) for all t>=T with cell(t,i)=0. In particular, if the center column c is eventually periodic, column 1 restricted to the white times of c is not eventually periodic (for any period that is a multiple of c's period). Also c(t)=1 implies cell(t,-1) = not c(t+1).
claims.proof: Left-permutivity gives cell(t,i-1) = cell(t+1,i) XOR (cell(t,i) OR cell(t,i+1)). For t>=T: cell(t+Q,i-1) = cell(t+Q+1,i) XOR (cell(t+Q,i) OR cell(t+Q,i+1)) = cell(t+1,i) XOR (cell(t,i) OR cell(t+Q,i+1)), using periodicity of column i at t+1 and t. If cell(t,i)=1 both OR terms are 1, so the value is cell(t,i-1). If cell(t,i)=0 the hypothesis gives cell(t+Q,i+1)=cell(t,i+1), so again the value is cell(t,i-1). Hence columns i-1 and i are both eventually Q-periodic, contradicting Jen's adjacent-column theorem (Rule30Jen.not_adjacent (i-1)). The last statement is the same identity at i=0 with cell(t,0)=1. Lean: R30NewIdeas.masked_jen, center_masked_not_eventually_periodic, left_of_black_center (axioms: propext, Quot.sound only).
claims.evidence: This is the sharp absorption criterion. With it, driver 0111 is absorbing: column 1 on its single white phase became periodic in 300/300 random right-half starts, although the full column 1 was periodic in only 12/300. This corrects the round-1 note that 0111 does not absorb.

This holds in every rule-30 evolution; it depends only on cells 1..11 at time t. Eight black steps do not suffice: for 112 of the 2048 right rows, cell 1 is black after 8 black steps.

Iterating 9 times with c=1, cells 1 and 2 at time t+9 are a function of cells 1..11 at time t. `decide` over all 2^11 rows returns [false,true] (black9_check). claims.statement: The center column of rule 30 is not eventually periodic if, from some time on, every white center cell lies in a white run preceded by at least 9 black cells. Equivalently, for an eventually periodic c, the repeating block cannot have all its cyclic black runs of length >= 9 (unless it has no white cell, the already excluded constant case). Corollary: for every k>=9, c is not eventually (0 1^k)^infinity, for any transient and any phase. The same holds for every block of the form 0^a 1^b with b>=9, and more generally.
claims.proof: Let z be the first white time of a white run that is preceded by >=9 blacks. By black-run-forcing, cell(z,1)=0 and cell(z,2)=1. So cell(z+1,1) = c(z) XOR (0 OR 1) = 1, and while c stays white, cell(s+1,1) = cell(s,1) OR cell(s,2) = 1. Hence for every large white time t, cell(t,1) = NOT c(t-1), which is eventually P-periodic because c is. Masked Jen with Q=P gives a contradiction. Lean: not_eventually_periodic_of_long_black_runs (general hypothesis form) and not_eventually_zero_ones (k>=9).
claims.evidence: Consistent with the strip-certificate scan: every word with all black runs >=9 is certified at width 5.

claims.statement: Strip-certificate soundness. Fix a word w of length P and a width b. Nodes are (phi,s) with phi in Z_P and s in {0,1}^b. Edges are (phi,s) -> (phi+1 mod P, lin3(w_phi :: s ++ [x])) for x in {0,1}; this is rule 30 at columns 1..b with column b+1 unknown. Suppose there is a rank function that does not increase along any edge, and a position labelling such that: on rank-preserving edges pos advances by 1 mod m_r exactly at white phases; at white phases column 1 equals u_r[pos]; and the counter map G(p,phi) = (p+[w_phi=0] mod m, phi+1) satisfies G^{mP}=id. Then the center column is not eventually w^infinity, for any transient. Kernel-checked instances, none covered by long-black-runs-excluded: w = 01111111 (b=5; black run 7), 00000011 (b=6), 0^10 1 (b=6), 000000000101 (b=7), 0011111111 (b=8; black run 8).
claims.proof: Assume c(t) = w[(t-T) mod P] for t>=T. By rowR_succ, the true strip history (cells 1..b at times >=T) is a path in the graph, with x = cell(t,b+1). Its rank is a non-increasing Nat sequence, so it is constant from some T' on (antitone_eventually_const). After T' every edge is rank-preserving. Hence (pos, phase) follows G, so q(t+mP) = q(t), and cell(t,1) = u_r[pos(t)] at every white t >= T'. Therefore cell(t+mP,1) = cell(t,1) at white t >= T', and c(t+mP) = c(t). Masked Jen with Q=mP gives the contradiction. Lean: Cert.sound (axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). Instances are discharged by `decide +kernel` on packed-Nat tables. Times: 1.6 s (01111111), 3.9 s (00000011), 12.6 s (0^10 1), 30 s (000000000101), 32 s (0011111111).
claims.evidence: Certificates were generated by cert.py, an independent Kosaraju implementation with an explicit edge-by-edge certificate check, and agree with the C scanner strip_scan.c.
claims.lean_plan: Framework: lean/StripCertCore.lean (also inside R30NewIdeasAll.lean). Instances: lean/Inst_c01111111.lean, Inst_c00000011.lean, Inst_c0x10_1.lean, Inst_c000000000101.lean, Inst_c0011111111.lean. New words are added with `python3 -I export_cert.py <w> <b> <name>` then `python3 -I make_instance.py <name> <w> <b>`. Kernel time grows roughly like (P*2^b)^2; packed tables keep it feasible up to about 2500 nodes.

claims.statement: Local forcing cannot exclude short periods. For every primitive period word w of length 2 to 7, and every strip width b<=16 (b<=20 for 0001), the strip graph has a strongly connected component containing two cycles whose outputs (column 1 at white phases) do not commute. Hence there are strip histories, with column b+1 unconstrained, along which column 1 on the white times is not eventually periodic. So no argument that uses the rule only at columns 1..b, even together with Jen and masked Jen, excludes any eventual period word of length 2..7, in particular periods 2, 3 and 4. Adding Jen-type constraints removes none of these bad components: forbidding any single strip column, or any masked pair (column p, column p+1 on the zeros of column p), from being periodic inside the component still leaves it (checked for 01 and 011 at b=10, and 0001 at b=12).
claims.proof: Exhaustive SCC computation: strip_scan.c for all primitive words with P<=12 at every b=2..12, P<=7 at every b=13..16, and 0001 at b=18 and 20. Cross-validated with Python (cert.py, strip_scc.py, jen_aug.py). Non-commuting cycle outputs alpha and beta give an aperiodic output along alpha beta alpha beta^2 alpha beta^3 ...; Fine-Wilf rules out eventual periodicity. This is a statement about the relaxation, not a construction of real rule-30 histories. Rigor rests on the code; the C and Python implementations agree on the component sizes checked.
claims.evidence: Bad-component sizes for 0001 are 318, 927, 2523, 6101, 14851, 34949 for b=10..20, growing about x1.5 per column. Projections onto columns 1-4, 1-6 and 1-8 are the same 13, 40 and 101 phase-patterns for every b=12..18, and proj(B_{b+2}) is a subset of B_b. This stable nested structure suggests that non-absorbing infinite (not finitely supported) right halves exist. The coordinator's round-1 adversarial computation for 0001 points the same way.

claims.statement: Conjecture (period-4 absorption). For w in {0001, 0011, 0111}, in every phase, and for every finitely supported initial right half, the right half driven by w^infinity has column 1 restricted to the white times eventually periodic. By masked Jen this would prove that the center column is not eventually periodic with least period 4, for any transient.

If c=w^infinity from T, then the true right half at time T is finitely supported and is driven by w^infinity, so column 1 on the white times would be eventually periodic, contradicting masked Jen. local-obstruction shows a proof must use finite support or edge structure, because finite strips with adversarial column b+1 can avoid absorption forever.

claims.proof: At black times, cell(t,-1) = not c(t+1) = 1. At white times the rule at column 0 gives cell(t,-1) = 1 XOR cell(t,1). Golden mean: if cell(z,-1)=0 then cell(z,1)=1, so cell(z+1,1) = 0 XOR 1 = 1 and cell(z+2,1) = 1 XOR 1 = 0, whence cell(z+2,-1)=1. Columns -2, -3 and -4 follow from the left reconstruction cell(t,i-1) = cell(t+1,i) XOR (cell(t,i) OR cell(t,i+1)). For column -4 at a white time: if cell(t+2,-1)=1 the value is 1 XOR 1; otherwise the golden mean forces cell(t,-1)=1 and the value is 0 XOR 0. Lean: Alt, alt_left_one, alt_right_even, alt_golden, alt_col2_even, alt_col2_odd, alt_col3_even, alt_col3_odd, alt_col4_even (axioms propext, Quot.sound).

A symbolic dependence analysis (p2_symbolic.py) shows the left columns x_n are sliding-block codes of u = column -1 at white times, with windows growing like n/2 (checked to n=27). So no bounded-memory, Jen-type contradiction is available.

claims.statement: The rule-30 evolutions of delta_0 (one black cell) and delta_0+delta_1 (two adjacent black cells) agree at every (t,p) with p <= t-1. In particular their center columns coincide. So the map 'finite configuration -> center column' is not injective, and injectivity cannot be the route to UPTC.
claims.proof: Measure right diagonals from each pattern's own right edge: R_j(t) = cell(t,t-j) for delta_0 and R'_j(t) = cell'(t,t+1-j) for delta_0+delta_1. Both satisfy R_{j+2}(t+1) = R_{j+2}(t) XOR (R_{j+1}(t) OR R_j(t)) with R_0 = R'_0 = 1, and R_j(0) = [j=0], R'_j(0) = [j in {0,1}]. Then R_1(t) = t mod 2 and R'_1 = not R_1. R'_2 and R_1 both satisfy x(t+1) = x(t) XOR 1 with x(0)=0, so R'_2 = R_1. R'_3(t+1) = R'_3(t) XOR (R_1 OR not R_1) = R'_3(t) XOR 1, and R_2(t+1) = R_2(t) XOR (R_1 OR 1) = R_2(t) XOR 1, both starting at 0, so R'_3 = R_2. By induction R'_{j+1} = R_j for all j>=1 (same recurrence, same inputs, initial value 0). Hence cell'(t,p) = R'_{t+1-p}(t) = R_{t-p}(t) = cell(t,p) whenever t+1-p >= 2, i.e. p <= t-1. Also checked numerically to t=3000.
claims.evidence: Seeds delta_0+delta_k with k>=3 do change the center column at t = 7, 8, 11, 18, ... .

claims.statement:
(a) For any target sequence c and any right half R (positions >=1), there is at most one left half L such that the configuration (L, c(0), R) has center column c. That L is the left reconstruction from columns 0 = c and -1, where col_{-1}(t) = c(t+1) XOR (c(t) OR col_1(t)) and col_1 is the right half started from R and driven by c.
(b) Problem 1 follows from the uniform periodic-trace conjecture (UPTC): no nonzero finite configuration has a purely periodic center column.

Left-permutivity reconstructs every column p <= -1 at all times >= 0 from columns 0 and -1, in particular the left half at time 0. (b) If c is periodic from T, then row T of the seed's evolution is a nonzero finite configuration whose center column is purely periodic.
claims.evidence: This reduction generalizes Condrey's period-1 method (arXiv 2609.09431). It shows the only obstruction for period P is finiteness of the left reconstruction from (w^infinity, sigma w XOR (w OR col_1(R))).

claims.statement:
For configurations of radius r, the maximal length of a center-column prefix equal to w^infinity is:
- P=1: exactly r+2 for w=1 and 2*ceil(r/2)+1 for w=0 (excluding the zero configuration), reproducing Condrey.
- P=2: 35 (w=01) and 36 (w=10) at r=20..22.
- P=3: 27-32 at r=20.
- P=4: 25-28 at r=20.
Growth is irregular, with doubling counts of maximizers. Left-only relaxation (LOP) for period 2: max horizon 53 for support size M=30, ratio about 1.7-1.9 for M<=30.

LOP horizons come from exhaustive DFS (lop.c). These are exact finite computations. Their interpretation (random-constraint behaviour, so no exact structure for P>=2) is heuristic.
claims.evidence: The ratios match a heuristic in which the right half's influence on column 0 travels left at speed about 1/4. Under this heuristic only about r/4 free bits remain by time r, predicting a ratio of about 4/3 for P=3,4. Data: trace_prefix and lop outputs in the scratch dir.

claims.statement: Uniform periodic-trace conjecture: no nonzero finitely supported configuration of rule 30 has a purely periodic center column. Equivalently, no column of any nonzero finite rule-30 orbit is eventually periodic. This implies Problem 1.

claims.statement: The left half driven by an arbitrary center column agrees with the true left half left of about -0.24t, except along accumulator diagonals that follow white stripes. There a single phase bit can flip and propagate at speed 1 along the diagonal; this was seen at diagonals 3 and 400, matching Rowland's period-doubling locations. Periodic drivers (01, 0001, 0011, 001, 0110111) spread their influence at the same speed, 0.21-0.25.
claims.proof: Empirical (left_universal.py, left_periodic_front.py, up to t=5000). Consistent with Rowland's Proposition 2: the period doubles exactly when a diagonal is eventually white and the diagonal to its left has odd parity per period. So the regular left region carries essentially no information about the center column. Periodic driving neither shrinks the chaotic region nor makes column -1 periodic.
claims.evidence: Random drivers: the front sits at -0.20t to -0.24t. One random driver flipped the accumulator at diagonal 400, after which the difference travels at speed 1 at fixed distance 400 from the edge.

result.failed_approaches:
Approaches tried and discarded:

1. Bounded-memory renormalization for period 2. Under alternation, the left columns are sliding-block codes of the golden-mean sequence u (column -1 at white times). The windows grow like n/2 (symbolic check to n=27), so information is never lost and a Jen-type bounded-window contradiction is impossible.

2. Finite-strip (local) forcing for short periods. This provably fails (local-obstruction): every word of length 2..7 has a bad SCC at every width up to 16, and 0001 up to width 20.

3. Jen-augmented strips. Requiring that no strip column, and no masked pair of columns, is periodic inside the SCC removes no bad SCC.

4. Pointwise forcing for long white runs (subset construction). Column 1 takes both values at most white phases. Only path-level SCC certificates work, so the forcing families are limited to black runs of at least 9.

5. Left-side absorption and the left-only relaxation (LOP). The left half has no local constraints: column -1 can be steered permutively from the left. The LOP faking horizon is about 1.8M, random-like, so a left-only proof would need a pseudo-randomness theorem. Periodic drivers spread leftward at the same speed (about 0.24) as random ones.

6. Injectivity of the map 'finite configuration -> center column' (would give UPTC). False: delta_0 and delta_0+delta_1 have the same center column (right-edge-insensitivity).

7. An exact two-sided classification of periodic center columns, as Condrey did for P=1. For P=2..4 the maximal faking prefix is irregular and random-like (about 1.25r-1.9r), not a closed formula.

8. Universal absorption over all right configurations. Likely false: the nested bad SCCs have stable projections. A real proof must use finite support.

9. Potential functions and conservation laws. Rule 30 has no GF(2)-linear conserved functional, because the quadratic term x(p)x(p+1) cannot cancel. The only monotone quantities found are local: column 1 under white input and the NOR dynamics under black input. These are exactly what the certificates already exploit.

10. Counting and entropy over the light cone. Every version reduces to 'free bits versus checks' heuristics with linear faking horizons. A single deterministic orbit cannot be excluded by counting.

11. Rowland's self-similarity. Right diagonals with periods 2^{e_j} replicate c(0..~2.3n) in column 2^n near the right edge. These are finite replicas and constrain nothing about the tail. The left period doubling is driver-independent apart from white-stripe phase bits.

12. Driving the halves by periodic words and hoping a second column becomes periodic. This works only for absorbing words, and even there absorption is non-local, except for saturating words with long runs.
result.most_promising_next_step:
The most promising next step is Program B: prove the period-4 absorption conjecture for finitely supported right halves. That would exclude least period 4 for every transient, the first full period beyond 1.

1. Compute the nested bad SCCs B_b (b -> infinity) of the 0001, 0011 and 0111 strip graphs. Dumps for 0001 at b=12..18 are in newideas/bad_0001_*.txt.
2. Extract the set of column-(b+1) input sequences that keep the strip inside B_b forever.
3. Test whether staying in every B_b forces an infinitely extended structure in the columns beyond b that a finitely supported right half cannot sustain. Its columns are born at the right edge with the rigid right-diagonal structure, and right-edge-insensitivity says that edge carries no information.
4. If such a structure is forced, the true strip must eventually enter the certified traps, and masked Jen finishes the proof.

In parallel, two cheaper steps would add guaranteed partial results:
- Make Program A uniform with a pumping lemma for long runs in `Cert`, so that 0^k 1 for all k>=10 and similar infinite families are kernel-checked.
- Move lean/R30NewIdeasAll.lean (masked_jen, Cert.sound, black_run, not_eventually_periodic_of_long_black_runs, the period-2 lemmas) and the Inst_*.lean certificates into ruliology-lean.

result.angle: Absorbing words, right half: drive the right half of rule 30 (cells p >= 1) at p = 0 by a periodic word w and ask when column 1 is eventually periodic from every starting configuration. Each such word rules out "c is eventually w-periodic" for every transient T, by Jen's theorem on columns 0 and 1.
result.summary:
This angle gives T-independent exclusions of infinite families of repeating words, several of them kernel-checked in Lean. It excludes no full period P >= 2.

**Mechanism.**
- **Lemma A (nine-black shield, Lean):** if a column is black for 9 consecutive steps, the next two columns are then (white, black).
- **Lemma A*:** 9j consecutive blacks force (white black)^j in the next 2j columns. So the "w = 1 lock" spreads into any configuration at speed 2/9 and blocks all leftward information.
- **Fact Z:** during a white run of the driver, column 1 is monotone and the leftmost black cell moves left by one column per step.

**Kernel-checked theorems** (scratch file `AbsorbRight.lean`; axioms only propext, Quot.sound):
- **Theorem B:** the center column is not eventually periodic with repeating word 1^r u when r >= 9*ceil((|u|+9)/2). For example, a black run of at least 0.82P + 8.2 in a period of length P is impossible.
- **Theorem B':** the same for r >= max(9, 9*j0(u)), where j0(u) is a finite check. SAT gives j0 <= 4 for all 64 blocks of length <= 7 (that start and end white), so a black run of length >= 36 followed by at most 7 other symbols is excluded. The check is kernel-verified for |u| <= 4; for example, 1^r 0 is excluded for every r >= 18.
- **Theorem D:** a black run of length >= 9 followed directly by a white run of length r >= 1 + 9*ceil((k+8)/2), where k is the rest of the period, is impossible. For example, 1^s 0^r is excluded for all s >= 9 and r >= 37.

**Also kernel-checked** (`AbsorbWhite.lean`, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound): the words 0^r 11 for r >= 10.

**SAT-assisted (CaDiCaL, not certified):**
- **Theorem C:** for each of the 64 blocks u of length <= 7 that start and end black, 0^r u is excluded for all r >= R(u), with R(u) <= 93. This uses a uniform-in-r reduction (the front-relative image sets shrink over time).
- **Exact thresholds:** 0^r 1 for r >= 10; 0^r 11 for r = 6 and r >= 8; 0^r 101 for r >= 11; 0^r 1111 for r >= 9.
- **Uniform-absorption certificates:** 00000011, 0000000011, 0011111111, and 1^r 0 for r >= 14.

**Structure.** In the experimentally absorbing words, column 1 ends up in a "lock": a time-periodic layer of columns 1..d bounded by a shield column. Shields found: 1^7 0 (12 steps of history) and 1^(Q-1) 0 for Q >= 10 (Lemma A). The leftward orbit of a shield lists the drivers that have a permanent lock:
- The orbit of 1^7 0 contains exactly the 7 absorbing words of length 8 and all 3 of length 4.
- The orbit of 1^9 0 contains all 14 absorbing words of length 10.
- For lengths 11 and 12, every orbit word at distance <= 17 is absorbing.

**Experimental classification** (all Lyndon words up to length 10, widths up to 3000, real right-edge starts):
- Absorbing: 0, 1; 0001, 0011, 0111; 7 words of length 8; 14 of length 10.
- No absorbing words at lengths 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, apart from the slow or partial cases 001 and 01111.
- 001 locks with period 21 at a width of 38 columns, after up to 7*10^4 steps.
- 01 has a permanent lock of width 14, but it is never reached in runs of 3*10^5 steps.

**Excluded periods.** Only P = 1 is fully excluded. The word 01 is not absorbing, so right-absorption alone cannot exclude any P >= 2.

**Non-uniformity.** For 0001, SAT finds starts whose lock forms arbitrarily late (a period-8 regime for column 1 holds for at least 160 steps first). So 0001, 0011 and 0111 stay conjectural.

claims.statement: (Lemma A) For any time t and column m of rule 30 (in fact of any rule-30 space-time pattern): if cell(t+s,m)=1 for s=0..8, then cell(t+9,m+1)=0 and cell(t+9,m+2)=1. Eight consecutive black cells do not suffice.
claims.proof:
Let row(t,p,n)=(cell(t,p),...,cell(t,p+n-1)), and let stepRow(l,(a0,...,ak)) = (rule(l,a0,a1), rule(a0,a1,a2), ..., rule(a_{k-2},a_{k-1},a_k)), where rule(x,y,z) = x xor (y or z).
1. By the definition of cell and induction on n: stepRow(cell(t,p-1), row(t,p,n+1)) = row(t+1,p,n).
2. If column m is black at times t..t+k-1, iterate step 1 with p=m+1 and left value true: runBlack_k(row(t,m+1,n+k)) = row(t+k,m+1,n), where runBlack applies stepRow(true,.) k times.
3. Take k=9, n=2: (cell(t+9,m+1), cell(t+9,m+2)) = runBlack_9(row(t,m+1,11)).
4. Exhaustive evaluation over all 2^11 rows of length 11 gives [false,true] every time. QED.

For 8 blacks, an exhaustive search over the 2^10 rows of length 10 finds rows with runBlack_8(row)_0 = true (144 of the 2^12 depth-11 cases of the shield check also fail).

claims.statement: (Theorem B) Let P >= 1 and T >= 0 with c(t+P) = c(t) for all t >= T, where c is the center column. Then no window [t1, t1+r) with t1 >= T and r <= P is all black with 9*ceil((P-r+9)/2) <= r. Equivalently, for every transient, c is not eventually periodic with repeating word (any rotation of) 1^r u where r >= 9*ceil((|u|+9)/2). For example, a black run of at least about 0.82P + 8.2 in the period is impossible.
claims.proof:
Let j = ceil((P-r+9)/2), so 2j >= P-r+9 and 9j <= r. Put e = t1+r and e_k = e+kP.
1. By periodicity, c is black on [e_k - r, e_k). Lemma A* at column 0 then shows that the row at e_k reads (0,1)^j on columns 1..2j, for every k.
2. The driver agrees: c(e+s) = c(e_k+s) for all s >= 0.
3. By the cone lemma, cell(e+s,1) = cell(e_k+s,1) for 0 <= s <= 2j-1, which covers s <= P-r+8.
4. For P-r+9 <= s <= P-1, the 9 times before e+s (and before e_k+s) lie in the next black run [e+P-r, e+P), which has length r. Lemma A gives cell(e+s,1) = cell(e_k+s,1) = 0.
5. So cell(e+kP+s,1) = cell(e+s,1) for all k and all 0 <= s < P. Column 1 is therefore periodic with period P from time e. Together with column 0 this contradicts Jen's theorem (Rule30Jen.not_adjacent 0).

claims.proof:
This proof is computer-assisted. The SAT answers come from CaDiCaL (the Lean 4.30 toolchain binary) and were not certified with DRAT/LRAT.
1. **Classes.** At each period start, let l be the index of the first black cell minus 1.
2. **Lock region, l <= r - 9j.** By Fact Z, column 1 is black on [l, r]. Lemma A* at column 1 gives the prefix 1(01)^j at the end of the white run. Applying u gives a fixed prefix whose first black is at l*+1, so l' = l* and the column-1 word of the period is fixed.
3. **Boundary classes, d = r - l in [-Z, 9j).** Take r0 = Z <= l. At time l - r0 the configuration is 0^r0 followed by a front-relative image Y.
   - The front-relative dynamics G is autonomous: G(1,Y) = (1, rule30 with a white left neighbour applied to Y). So the reachable sets Im_n = G^n(all) decrease in n.
   - The rest of the period is exactly one period of W' = 0^(r0+d) u started in class r0. So the set of next classes is contained in the set computed for W' with arbitrary tails, a finite SAT problem on the light cone.
   - Classes l > r+Z reduce in the same way to W'' = 0^r0 u with zeros on columns 1..r0+Z+1.
4. **Bound.** CaDiCaL computes the maximal next class over all cases (by witness iteration until UNSAT); call it B, which includes l*.
5. **Conclusion.** For r >= max(r0 + 9j, B + 9j), every configuration has l <= B <= r - 9j after one period. It is then in the lock from the next period on, so column 1 is periodic. Jen gives the contradiction.

claims.statement:
(Lock permanence via shields) Call a period-Q column pattern sigma a shield with depth n and forced values f if, in every rule-30 evolution where column m equals sigma (aligned) at times t-n..t-1 and sigma(t)=0, we have cell(t,m+1) = f(t mod Q).
Define the leftward orbit by C_0 = sigma and C_{i+1}(tau) = C_i(tau+1) xor (C_i(tau) or C_{i-1}(tau)), where C_{-1} = f at the zeros of sigma.
If the driver equals C_d and the right half agrees with the lock (column j = C_{d-j}, j = 1..d) at n+1 consecutive times, it agrees forever, so column 1 is periodic.
Verified shields:
- sigma_8 = 1^7 0 with depth 12 (exhaustive over 2^13 cone configurations; depth 11 fails in 144 cases);
- sigma_Q = 1^(Q-1) 0 for every Q >= 10, with depth 9 and f = 0 (by Lemma A);
- sigma_Q is NOT a shield for Q <= 7 or Q = 9 (SAT, depth up to 60).
claims.proof:
Induct on time t, assuming agreement at times t-n..t; show agreement at t+1.
1. **Columns j < d.** cell(t+1,j) = rule(cell(t,j-1), cell(t,j), cell(t,j+1)), all locked, and this matches the orbit relation C_i(tau+1) = C_{i+1}(tau) xor (C_i(tau) or C_{i-1}(tau)).
2. **Column d where sigma(t) = 1.** The new value is C_1(t) xor 1 = sigma(t+1).
3. **Column d where sigma(t) = 0.** The shield property applies, because column d = sigma on [t-n, t-1] by the induction hypothesis. It gives cell(t,d+1) = f(t), so the new value is C_1(t) xor f(t) = sigma(t+1) by the definition of C_1.

So max Z_{t+1} <= max Z_t, with equality only if the value at (t, max Z_t) is 1. Periodicity makes the maximum a constant m, so column m is black at all times. Since rule(x,1,.) = not x, column m-1 is white at all times, column m-2 is black, and so on down to column 0. That makes the driver constant, a contradiction.

result.failed_approaches:
1. **Arbitrary-input strip automaton.** Columns 1..k with an arbitrary right input, then an SCC test for eventually periodic column-1 output. It fails for every nonconstant word for k <= 12. The no_static_shield lemma explains part of this: no one-step-determined shield exists for nonconstant drivers.

2. **Exact image languages.** These are minimal DFAs of the n-step reachable configurations. For 00000011 the DFA sizes are 7, 50, 1003, 24551, 836096 for n = 1..5, so the approach is infeasible.

3. **Backward preimage sets of the 'bad event'.** These work for shield depth (1^7 0: 12) but blow up for longer patterns; SAT is the better tool.

4. **Uniform SAT test** (column 1 forced to be Q-periodic from a fixed N0 for all configurations). It succeeds only for 00000011, 0000000011, 0011111111 and 1^r 0 (r >= 14). It fails for 0001, 0011, 0111, 00000001, 0000000001, 001 and others. The reason is that lock formation time is unbounded: there are competing metastable locks, e.g. a period-8 column-1 regime for 0001.

5. **Leftmost-1 (front-position) abstraction.** It proves long white-run words but fails for short words and for 0^7 1 and 0^9 1, although these are experimentally absorbing.

6. **Hand proof of the general white-run theorem.** Late-front boundary cases depend on unknown cells; a bound was obtained only via SAT (|u| <= 7).

7. **Kernel decide of Determined(u, j0) for all 64 blocks.** The list encoding takes 15-60 s per |u| = 7 block, so the kernel instances were done only for |u| <= 4.

8. **Right-absorption for period 2 (driver 01).** A permanent lock exists but is never approached; the locked prefix stays <= 5 of 14 columns.

I found no essential gap. The non-essential issues are:
(1) The "Equivalently" sentence names the wrong edge case. An all-black block is covered by the main theorem itself, because its hypothesis is vacuously true and masked Jen still applies. The block not covered is the all-white one: it vacuously has "all cyclic black runs >= 9", but its white cells are not preceded by blacks, so the hypothesis fails. That case is excluded by the separate, already-proved theorem center_not_eventually_constant. So the statement is true, but it is not literally an equivalence for the all-white block.
(2) Only the general-hypothesis form and the (0 1^k), k>=9 instance are in Lean. The step from "block w has both colours and every cyclic black run >= 9" to the Lean hypothesis is not formalised. That covers 0^a 1^b with a>=1, b>=9, and arbitrary blocks. I checked the step by hand: with T' = T+P+9, the last black s-1 before a white time t satisfies s-1 >= t-P >= T+9. The maximal black run of the periodic extension that ends at s-1 is a cyclic run of w, so it has length >= 9, and s-9 >= T, so c(s-9..s-1) = 1. Also k+10 <= t holds. The step is elementary but unformalised.
(3) I did not verify the cited evidence that every such word is certified by the width-5 strip scan. It is not load-bearing.
(4) Scope: this is a partial result. It excludes a family of repeating blocks for every transient and phase. It is not Problem 1.
(5) The threshold 9 is sharp for the forcing lemma: after 8 black steps, (col1, col2) = (1, 0) is still possible. So this method does not reach runs of 8 without new input.
(6) Integration: masked_jen is defined in both BlackRun.lean and MaskedJen.lean in namespace R30NewIdeas, so the two files clash if imported together. The same result was also proved in parallel as R30SmallPeriods.no_period_long_ones (verify-C3-longones).

The claim survives. I rebuilt every step of Theorem B and found each one rigorous.

Setup: with r <= P, the subtraction P-r is exact, so j = ceil((P-r+9)/2) = (P-r+10)/2 satisfies 2j >= P-r+9, 9j <= r and j >= 5.

(A) Absorbing pair. If the driver is 1 and columns (1,2) read (0,1), the next step is again (0,1): 1 xor 1 = 0 and 0 xor (1 or z) = 1.

(B) Pair lemma. If column m is black for 9 consecutive steps, then right after them columns m+1, m+2 read (0,1). The result depends only on the 11 starting cells to the right, so it is a finite check, and I re-ran it independently in Python over all 2^11 rows. 9 steps are needed: 8 steps fail for 56 rows. The single-cell form ("column 1 is white") also needs exactly 9.

(C) Lemma A*. If column 0 is black on [e-9j, e), then row e reads (0,1)^j on columns 1..2j. Proof by induction on the pair index i, using translation invariance. Column 2i-2 stays black from t0+9(i-1) to e by the previous step, so (B) settles pair i at t0+9i and (A) keeps it settled until e. I also checked this directly for j=1 and j=2 over all 2^11 and 2^22 rows, and 9j-1 steps fail in both cases.

(D) Steps 1-2. Periodicity from T gives black on [t1+kP, t1+kP+r) for every k, and c(e+s) = c(e_k+s) for s >= 0. Applying (C) gives the (0,1)^j pattern at every e_k.

(E) Cone. cell(e+s,1) depends only on row e at columns 1..1+s and on the driver values c(e..e+s-1), by induction on s. So columns agree for s <= 2j-1, which covers s <= P-r+8.

(F) Remaining s, from 2j up to P-1. These satisfy s >= P-r+9, so the 9 times before e+s fall inside the next run [t1+P, t1+P+r), and likewise for e_k+s. By (B), column 1 is 0 at both times.

(G) Conclusion. Column 1 satisfies cell(t+P,1) = cell(t,1) for all t >= e, by division with remainder. Column 0 is P-periodic from T. Jen's adjacent case then gives the contradiction: rule 30 is left-permutive, so two adjacent periodic columns force every column to the left to be periodic, which the left edge forbids.

The "equivalently" form is also right: a period that is a rotation of 1^r u contains a black window starting at some t1 >= T, with P-r = |u|.

An exhaustive Python check of all 2^11 rows found 0 failures, and 9 is the smallest number of black steps that works.

(A*) Lemma A*: if column m is black for 9j consecutive steps, the next 2j columns read (01)^j right after. Proof by induction on j, for all t at once. The cases i <= j follow from the induction hypothesis started at t+9. For i = j+1, applying the induction hypothesis at starts t+s', s' < 9, makes column m+2j black at t+9j..t+9j+8. Lemma A on that column then gives the new pair.

Steps 1-2: Lemma A on the 9 blacks before e_k gives (cell(e_k,1), cell(e_k,2)) = (0,1). Then rule(0,0,1)=1 and rule(0,1,x)=1, so column 1 is black at e_k+1..e_k+r.

Step 3: the window [f_k-9j, f_k) lies inside [e_k+1, e_k+r] exactly when r >= 9j+1, which is the hypothesis. Lemma A* at m=1 then gives (01)^j on columns 2..2j+1 at f_k, and column 1 is black at f_k.

Step 4: the cone lemma states that if two rows agree on columns 1..n and column 0 agrees from then on, then the cells agree wherever p >= 1 and p+x <= n. It follows by induction on x, using column 0 as the left neighbour of column 1. Here column 0 agrees because c(f_0+x) = c(f_k+x), as f_0 >= T. With n = 2j+1 this makes cell(f_k+x, 1) the same for every k when x <= 2j.

Step 5: Lemma A makes column 1 white on [b_{k+1}+9, e_{k+1}].

Coverage of offsets i in [0, P): i=0 is white by step 1; 1 <= i <= r is black; r < i <= r+2j is fixed by the cone; r+2j < i < P is white. The last case holds because r+2j+1 >= r+K+9 = P-s+9 (this is where 2j >= K+8 is needed), and P-s+9 is offset b_{k+1}+9.

result.verdict_summary:
The claim holds. I rebuilt the proof from the statement and sketch, and every step is rigorous.

Setup: P = r+|u| and e_k = t1+r+kP. By periodicity (t1 >= T), column 0 is black on [e_k-r, e_k), equals u on [e_k, e_k+|u|), and is black again on [e_k+|u|, e_k+|u|+r).

1. **Lemma A.** If column m is black for 9 consecutive steps, then at the next step columns m+1 and m+2 read white, black. This is a finite check: those two cells depend only on 11 cells of the starting row plus the black driver, and all 2^11 cases pass. Python agrees, and also shows that 8 steps are not enough.
2. **Lemma A\*.** By induction on j, 9j black steps force (white black)^j on the next 2j columns. In the inductive step, the IH applied at start t+s (s <= 8) makes column m+2j black for 9 consecutive steps, and then Lemma A applies. Since 9*j0 <= r, the row at every e_k starts with (white black)^j0.
3. **Light cone.** Column 1 at time e+s depends only on the row at time e (columns 1..s+1) and on column 0 during [e, e+s).
4. **Trace fixed.** The driver from e_k is u then 1^9, which uses r >= 9. The row at e_k is (white black)^j0 followed by some tail, which uses 2*j0 <= |u|+10. So `Determined(u,j0)` gives the same column-1 trace for every k at offsets s = 0..|u|+9.
5. **Rest of the period.** For |u|+9 <= s <= P, the 9 cells before e_k+s lie in the next black run, so Lemma A makes column 1 white there.
6. **Contradiction.** So cell(e_k+s, 1) = cell(e_0+s, 1) for all k and all s < P. Column 1 is then P-periodic from e_0, and column 0 is P-periodic from T. Jen's adjacent-columns theorem rules this out. It follows from left-permutivity, which spreads periodicity to every column on the left, and the left edge, where cell(-t, -t) = 1 and everything further left is 0.

The Lean proof `no_black_run_block` follows exactly this structure. Its statement matches the claim: any period P = r+|u| from any T, any phase t1 >= T, with r >= 9 and 9*j0 <= r. The definitions are correct for rule 30 (`rule a b c = a xor (b || c)`, single black seed), and nothing in the files weakens checking (no sorry, no skipped kernel checks, only a linter option).

Overall, Theorem B′ is kernel-checked, its stated instances are kernel-checked, the j0 table is confirmed by exhaustive computation in two independent evaluators (Python and Lean's `#eval`), and the r >= 36 corollary is kernel-checked for every word of length at most 7.

result.status_of_problem_1:
OPEN. As of 2026-10-15 no proof exists anywhere, and round 1 did not change that.

Literature. The four literature surveys found every claimed solution invalid: Das 2022, Basta 2025, Fradkin 2026, Brauer 2025, Deva 2025/26 and Tan Kian Cheng 2026. Each has a fatal gap, and most would also 'prove' false statements for rules 90, 150 or 22, or for Condrey's constant-trace configurations. rule30prize.org lists no winners. Kopra (TCS 2023, Problem 4.8 / 3.10) and Condrey (arXiv 2609.09431, Sept 2026) both state that the problem is open.

Rigorous frontier. 'Lean' means kernel-checked with standard axioms only.
- Period 1 is excluded for every transient (Lean). Condrey proves this for every nonzero finite configuration.
- Jen: at most one column is eventually periodic (Lean). Kopra: no nonzero left-bounded configuration has two adjacent eventually periodic columns.
- Bounded windows: no eventual period P ≤ 4096 with transient ≤ 8192 (Lean); every eventual period has T+P ≥ 16359 (Lean). From data only, not formal: no P ≤ 2.5·10^8 with T ≤ 5·10^8.
- New in round 1, adversarially verified and in Lean, for every transient and phase:
  - every period word that contains a white cell and whose cyclic black runs all have length ≥ 9;
  - every word with a single black run of length r ≥ 9⌈(P−r+9)/2⌉ (about 0.82P + 8.2);
  - every word made of a black run of length ≥ 36 plus at most 7 other symbols;
  - a black run of length ≥ 9 followed directly by a white run of length ≥ 1 + 9⌈(k+8)/2⌉;
  - 0^r 11 for r = 6 and every r ≥ 8;
  - 33 further specific words of length 8–13 via kernel-checked strip certificates (about 180 more certified by computer).
- Reductions (Lean):
  - Problem1 ⇔ no nonempty word is an eventual period word (problem1_iff_no_word).
  - 'c is not eventually 2-periodic' follows from Q01: no finite start of the zero-boundary left half keeps column −1 black at every even step.
  - 'no least period 4' follows from trap entry for 0001, 0011 and 0111; the conditional no-entry theorems are proved.
- Barriers (proved):
  - Rules 90, 150 and 210 share every structural ingredient used so far, yet have eventually periodic single-seed centres.
  - Every eventually periodic column is realized by some infinite configuration.
  - Strip and local certificates cannot exclude any word of length 2–7.
  - Left absorption is impossible.

Not achieved: no full period P ≥ 2 is excluded, and no nonconstant period word of length ≤ 7 is excluded. The first open cases are:
- period 2, the word 01, which is equivalent to showing c(t) = c(t+1) for infinitely many t;
- period 3, the words 001 and 011;
- least period 4, the words 0001, 0011 and 0111.

The problem is exactly as open as before round 1, but the frontier is now mapped sharply and the map is machine-checked.

verified_results.proof_outline: Rule 30 is left-permutive: cell(t,i−1) = cell(t+1,i) ⊕ (cell(t,i) ∨ cell(t,i+1)). Suppose columns i and i+1 are P-periodic from a common T. By induction every column q ≤ i is P-periodic from T. Pick q < −(T+P). At time −q the left edge gives cell(−q,q) = 1. At time −q−P ≥ T, position q lies outside the light cone, so cell(−q−P,q) = 0. This contradicts periodicity. For non-adjacent columns i < j, the strip strictly between them is a finite-state system driven by two periodic boundaries, so pigeonhole makes column i+1 eventually periodic and the adjacent case applies.

verified_results.statement: Masked Jen (Lean; adversarially verified). For any column i there are no T and Q > 0 such that column i is Q-periodic from T and column i+1 satisfies cell(t+Q,i+1) = cell(t,i+1) at every t ≥ T with cell(t,i) = 0. Equivalently: if column i is eventually Q-periodic, then column i−1 is eventually Q-periodic iff column i+1, restricted to the white times of column i, is. For the centre: if c is eventually periodic, then column 1 at the white times of c is not eventually periodic for any multiple of c's period; also c(t) = 1 ⇒ cell(t,−1) = ¬c(t+1). This is exactly Jen's adjacent case restated, not a strengthening. It is the precise target any 'absorption' argument must reach.

Otherwise the hypothesis replaces cell(t+Q,i+1) by cell(t,i+1). So column i−1 is Q-periodic from T, and columns i−1 and i contradict Jen.
