verified_results.statement:
Nine-black lemma, shield growth and cone agreement (Lean; verified).
- In any rule-30 space-time pattern, if column m is black at times t,...,t+8, then cell(t+9,m+1) = 0 and cell(t+9,m+2) = 1.
- If column m is black at times t,...,t+9j−1, then at time t+9j columns m+1,...,m+2j read (01)^j.
- The constants are optimal. After 8 black steps, 56 of the 1024 right windows are not absorbed, and 17 and 26 steps fail for j = 2 and 3. Eight steps also fail in the single-seed pattern: column 91 is black at t = 100..107, yet (cell(108,92), cell(108,93)) = (1,0).
- Cone agreement: if column 0 agrees at times t0+s and t1+s for all s ≥ 0, and the rows at t0 and t1 agree on columns 1..n, then cell(t0+s,p) = cell(t1+s,p) for p ≥ 1 and p+s ≤ n.
verified_results.proof_outline: While column m is black, the two target cells depend only on cells m+1..m+11 at time t (light cone with the left input fixed to 1); an exhaustive check over all 2^11 rows settles Lemma A. Lemma A* follows by induction on j: the inner pairs come from the window starting at t+9, and the new pair comes from Lemma A applied to column m+2j, which the induction hypothesis keeps black for 9 consecutive steps. The cone lemma is an induction on s, with column 0 serving as the left neighbour of column 1.
verified_results.lean_target: Done: staged Rule30BlackRuns (nine_black, nine_black_core, eight_black_not_enough, black_shield, cone_agree); verifier verify-lemmaA-nine-black-rigor/GenericLemmaA.lean (the lemma for any spacetime satisfying the rule).

verified_results.statement: Long-black-runs exclusion (Lean, two independent proofs; verified). The centre column is not eventually periodic with any period word that contains a white cell and whose cyclic maximal black runs all have length ≥ 9, for any transient and any phase. Examples: 0 1^k for k ≥ 9, and 0^a 1^b for a ≥ 1, b ≥ 9. Contrapositive: any nonconstant eventual period word would contain a black run of length ≤ 8 followed by a white cell. Finitary form: suppose c is P-periodic on a stretch starting at time a, has a 1 in every length-P window there, and every black run followed by a white cell has length ≥ 9. Then the stretch has length < a + 4P + 20.
verified_results.proof_outline: At the first white cell z of a white run preceded by ≥ 9 blacks, Lemma A gives (cell(z,1), cell(z,2)) = (0,1). Then cell(z+1,1) = 0 ⊕ (0 ∨ 1) = 1, and while c stays white, cell(s+1,1) = cell(s,1) ∨ cell(s,2) = 1. So cell(t,1) = ¬c(t−1) at every late white time t. Hence cell(t,−1) = c(t+1) ⊕ (c(t) ∨ ¬c(t−1)) is eventually P-periodic, and Jen (masked Jen) gives the contradiction.
verified_results.lean_target: Done: staged Rule30BlackRuns (not_eventuallyPeriodic_of_long_one_runs(_col), finitary_long_runs, not_eventually_zero_ones); smallperiods/lean/LongOnes.lean (no_period_long_ones); verifier verify-longblack-rederive/Rederive.lean (block_form, not_eventually_zeros_ones). Target: a List-Bool form ¬EventuallyWord w for every w with a white cell and all cyclic black runs ≥ 9.

verified_results.statement: Theorem B (Lean; verified). Suppose c(t+P) = c(t) for all t ≥ T. Then there is no all-black window [t1,t1+r) with t1 ≥ T, r ≤ P and 9⌈(P−r+9)/2⌉ ≤ r. A sufficient condition is r ≥ (9P+90)/11, about 0.82P + 8.2; the smallest admissible r is 45. So no eventual period word has a black run filling about 82% or more of the period.
verified_results.proof_outline: Let j = ⌈(P−r+9)/2⌉ and e_k = t1 + r + kP. Lemma A* puts (01)^j on columns 1..2j at every e_k. The centre column agrees from each e_k on, so the cone lemma makes column 1 agree for 2j ≥ P−r+9 steps. From 9 steps into the next black run, Lemma A makes column 1 white. Hence column 1 is P-periodic from e_0, contradicting Jen.
verified_results.lean_target: Done: staged Rule30BlackRuns.no_long_black_run.

verified_results.statement: Theorem B′ and its full table (Lean; verified; all 64 table entries kernel-checked). Let u be a block and j0 a number with 2j0 ≤ |u|+10 and Determined(u,j0), a finite check that every row starting (01)^{j0} gives the same column-1 trace under the driver u·1^9. Then 1^r u is excluded for every r ≥ max(9, 9·j0) and every transient. For all 64 blocks of length 1–7 that start and end white, j0(u) ≤ 4: 20 blocks have j0 = 2, 41 have 3 and 3 have 4. Determined(v,4) holds for all 255 words of length ≤ 7. Corollary: no eventual period word consists of a black run of length ≥ 36 plus at most 7 other symbols. For example, 1^r 0 is excluded for every r ≥ 18.
verified_results.proof_outline: As for Theorem B, except that a finite determination check over the non-black part of the period replaces the cone argument there.
verified_results.lean_target: Done: staged Rule30BlackRunBlocks (no_black_run_block plus 8 instances, no_period_black_run_then_white); verifier verify-Bprime-rigor (the other 56 Determined facts, mods/FinalN13.lean); verify-thmBprime-rederive/allw/W_All.lean (det4_upto7, no_black_run_plus_seven). Target: merge these into staging.

verified_results.statement: Theorem D (Lean; verified). Suppose c is P-periodic from T. Then no period window contains a black run of length s ≥ 9 followed immediately by a white run of length r ≥ 1 + 9⌈(k+8)/2⌉, where k = P−s−r; the runs need not be maximal. Example: 1^s 0^r is excluded for all s ≥ 9 and r ≥ 37.
verified_results.proof_outline: At the end of each black run, Lemma A puts (0,1) in columns 1 and 2. Column 1 then turns black and stays black through the white run, because rule(0,1,x) = 1. Lemma A*, applied to column 1, fixes 1(01)^j at the end of the white run. Cone agreement covers the next 2j ≥ k+8 steps, and Lemma A makes column 1 white for the rest of the period. So column 1 is P-periodic, contradicting Jen.
verified_results.lean_target: Done: staged Rule30BlackRuns.no_black_white_run.

verified_results.statement: The words 0^r 11 (Lean; verified). c is not eventually periodic with period word 0^r 11 (any rotation) for r = 6 and every r ≥ 8, for every transient. The case r = 7 is open (experimentally the right half does not absorb), as are r ≤ 5.
verified_results.proof_outline: Track the first black cell to the right of column 0 at the start of each white run; one exists because the right edge has cell(t,t) = 1. During a white run this front moves left one cell per step, and column 1 stays black once it turns black. For r ≥ 10, a case analysis on the front position shows that a self-sustaining lock forms within two periods, with column 1 reading 1^{r+1}0 (sustained by Lemma A). For r = 8 and 9, a finer case analysis on the front classes shows column 1 is eventually periodic in every branch. In all cases Jen gives the contradiction. The case r = 6 (word 00000011) is a kernel-checked strip certificate.

verified_results.statement:
Strip certificates (Lean soundness, kernel-checked instances) and their proven limit (computer-verified).
- Soundness: for a word w and width b, consider the graph on (phase, columns 1..b), with column b+1 a free input. Suppose there is a rank function that never increases along edges, and a position labelling that advances exactly at white phases on rank-preserving edges and determines column 1 there, with the counter map satisfying G^{mP} = id. Then w is excluded for every transient and phase.
- Kernel-checked exclusions: 33 words of length 8–13, including 00000011, 01111111, 0^{10}1, 000000000101, 0011111111, 00000001111 and the 30-word certTable. About 180 further words, including the families 0^k 1 for 10 ≤ k ≤ 30 and 0 1^k, are certified by two independent programs.
- Limit: for every primitive word of length 2–7 there is no such certificate at strip widths ≤ 16 (≤ 20 for 0001), and none for length 9 at widths ≤ 16. Each such strip graph has a strongly connected component containing two cycles whose column-1 outputs at white phases do not commute. So local and strip methods cannot exclude any of periods 2–7.
verified_results.proof_outline: Soundness: the true strip history from the onset is an infinite path in the graph, since the true column b+1 is one of the free inputs. Its rank is a non-increasing sequence of naturals, hence eventually constant. After that the labels follow the counter map, so column 1 at white times is eventually mP-periodic, contradicting masked Jen. The negative statement is an exhaustive SCC computation, cross-checked by newideas strip_scan.c and cert.py, smallperiods reach3.c and reach_py2.py, and generalize-jen strip_scc.c; three verifiers reproduced the counts.
verified_results.lean_target: Done: staged Rule30StripCertificates (Cert.sound, not_eventually_word_strip, problem1_iff_no_word, not_eventually_00000011, not_eventually_01111111) and Rule30StripCertificateTable.not_eventually_certTable; verifier verify-C4-counterexample/lean/C4a–C4c.lean. Target: one kernel-checked census table of all certified words up to length ~16.

verified_results.statement: Driven-left Jen, hence no left absorption (Lean; verified for every depth). Let the left half evolve by rule 30 with column 0 fed by any eventually periodic sequence, from a nonzero left-finite start. Then no column −m (m ≥ 1) is eventually periodic. Consequences: no word is left-absorbing, and the round-1 observation that the driven column −1 stays aperiodic is a theorem. Any word exclusion must therefore come from the right half (column 1 at white times) or from a genuinely global argument.
verified_results.proof_outline: Run Jen's argument inside the half-line. Left-permutivity holds at every p ≤ −1, with the driver as column 0. The leftmost black cell moves left one cell per step with only white beyond it, so two adjacent eventually periodic columns (column 0 included) are impossible. The strip between column −m and column 0 is finite-state, so pigeonhole makes column −m+1 eventually periodic, which reduces to the adjacent case.
verified_results.lean_target: Done: staged Rule30DrivenLeft (no_periodic_column, col_neg_one_not_periodic); verifier verify-driven-left-jen/DrivenLeftJen.lean (claim, seed_word).

verified_results.proof_outline: Existence: build the configuration as above and check the rule by induction on time, using xor cancellation at column 0 and at each reconstructed column. Uniqueness: equal right halves and equal centre columns give equal right halves at all times; the left-permutive identity then gives equal columns −1, −2, ... in turn.
verified_results.lean_target: Done: staged Rule30Realization (realize, unique, column_realizable_unique, seed_perturbation), from complexity/lean/Rule30Realize.lean. Target: adversarial review (round-2 r2-verify, item A2).

verified_results.statement: Barrier from rules 90, 150 and 210 (Lean, kernel-checked; standard). Consider the rules new = left ⊕ g(centre, right) with g(0,0) = 0 and g(0,1) = 1; this class is exactly rules 30, 90, 150 and 210. Every rule in it satisfies Jen's adjacent-column theorem, and its right diagonals carry the same 2-power period and 2-adic odometer structure. Yet from a single seed the centres of rules 90 and 210 are 1,0,0,..., and the centre of rule 150 is identically 1. Rule 210's seed orbit equals rule 90's, and rule 90 is also rapidly left-expansive in Kopra's sense. So a proof of Problem 1 must use rule 30's OR, i.e. g(1,0) = g(1,1) = 1, together with finiteness. Left-permutivity, the light cone, Jen, diagonal periodicity, nonlinearity, asymmetry or ANF degree are not enough, alone or combined.
verified_results.proof_outline: Jen's argument goes through with ⊕g in place of ⊕(c∨r). Rule 90: the seed orbit is supported on t+p even and cell(2t,2p) = cell(t,p), so the centre is 0 at odd times and center(2s) = center(s). Rule 150: cell(2t,2p) = cell(t,p) and cell(2t,2p+1) = 0, so the centre is identically 1 (central trinomial coefficients are odd). Rule 210 differs from rule 90 only when centre = right = 1, which never happens on rule 90's checkerboard support.
verified_results.lean_target: Done: staged Rule30Realization (barrier, run_not_adjacent, center90, center150, run210_eq, center210); gf2-algebra/lean/LeftPermutiveBarrier.lean.

verified_results.statement:
Right-diagonal period structure (Lean; verified). Let R_j(t) = cell(t,t−j), with least period 2^{e_j}.
(a) e_j ≤ e_{j+1} = e_j + R_{j+1}(2^{e_j}); when the period doubles, R_{j+1}(t+2^{e_j}) = ¬R_{j+1}(t). For j ≥ 3, e_j − e_{j−1} is the parity of R_{j−1} ∨ R_{j−2} over its least period 2^{e_{j−1}}; this proves the brief's empirical rule.
(b) R_0..R_n all have period 2^k iff row 2^k has at least n white cells immediately left of its right edge. Row N = 2^k·u with u odd reads, leftwards from the edge, 1 0^{J_k} 1, where J_k = max{j : e_j ≤ k}. Values: J_0..J_37 = 0 2 3 5 6 8 14 15 23 24 26 28 33 35 36 38 40 42 47 48 50 53 54 57 59 62 63 65 68 69 71 73 76 78 79 81 83 85, which extends e_j to j = 85 (e_85 = 37). Row 2^k−1 ends in exactly J_k+1 black cells, and k ≤ J_k ≤ 2^{k+1}−2.
(c) Restart: cell(N+s,N+q) = cell(s,q) whenever 0 ≤ s−q ≤ J_{ν2(N)}; so column 2^k·u repeats c(0..J_k).
(d) c(t) = 1 ⇒ 2^{e_t} > t: black centre cells lie in the first period of their diagonal. Also log2(j+2)−1 ≤ e_j ≤ (2j+1)/3, and the period never doubles three times in a row.
(e) The right-edge orbit closure is conjugate to the 2-adic odometer; the same holds for rules 60, 90, 150 and 210. Mahler and linear-complexity form: L_j = L(R_{j−1} ∨ R_{j−2}) + 1, e_j = ⌈log2 L_j⌉, and L_j = 2^{e_j−1}+1 at each period jump.
These facts relate c(t) only to cells exponentially far away, and rules with periodic centres share them, so they cannot decide Problem 1.
verified_results.proof_outline: (a) A halving lemma: if R_{j+1} has period H, the white light-cone cells of R_{j+1} force the lower diagonals white at time H, by descent; this gives monotonicity. The accumulator lemma x(t+L) = x(t) ⊕ x(L) ⊕ x(0) gives the shift formula. (b) and (c) follow from (a) and R_i(2^k) = cell(2^k, 2^k−i). (d) If 2^{e_t} ≤ t, then r = t mod 2^{e_t} satisfies 2r < t, so R_t(r) = 0 by the light cone. (e) The right-edge map G is a triangular isometry, and ψ(α)_j = R_j(α mod 2^{e_j}) is continuous, injective and equivariant on Z_2.
verified_results.lean_target: Done: staged Rule30RightPeriods (halve, per_mono_all, shift_formula, antiperiod, per_step, zero_gap, last_one, restart, column_continuity, center_black_lt, no_three, per_upper, per_14, per_23, rows_at_powers_of_two, e_step, S_rule); gf2-algebra/lean/Rule30DiagonalPeriods.lean (R_period_iff, right_end_copy); verify-B-odometer-rigor/EvenDiagPeriod.lean.

The forbidden pair words come from exhaustive checks over all right-half windows of the light cone (2^6, 2^10, 2^13 and 2^15 rows). verified_results.statement: Period-4 traps, conditional statements (Lean; verified). For w ∈ {0001, 0011, 0111} there are explicit sets S_w of right-strip states, of widths 16, 16 and 14 with 109, 188 and 188 states. Each set is closed under every value of the column beyond the strip, and on it column 1 at the white phases is a fixed function of the phase. Hence, if c is eventually w-periodic (in any phase), the true strip never enters S_w after the onset. Smaller traps exist: width 15 for 0011 and width 13 for 0111. Random finite right halves always enter: all of more than 4000 starts, after about 50–800 steps, independent of width. But adversarial strip inputs can avoid every trap forever. So excluding least period 4 needs a trap-entry theorem that uses the finiteness of the true right half.
verified_results.proof_outline: Closure and output consistency are finite checks (decide +kernel). Once the strip is inside the trap, column 1 at white times is periodic, contradicting masked Jen.
verified_results.lean_target: Done: verify-p4traps-rigor/P4Traps.lean (trap_sound, no_entry0001, no_entry0011, no_entry0111). Open target: for every finite right half driven by w^∞, the strip state lies in S_w at some time.

verified_results.statement: White seed and rule 135 (Lean, kernel-checked; elementary). Start rule 30 from all black except one white cell. Then cellW(t+1,p) = cell(t,p−1), so this centre column is column −1 of the usual pattern delayed by one step. By Jen, the centre column is not eventually periodic from the single black cell, or from the single white cell, or both. Equivalently, Problem 1 holds for rule 30 or for its conjugate rule 135 (and likewise for the mirrors 86 and 149).
verified_results.proof_outline: One step from the white seed gives a single black cell at position 1; the rest is induction on time. If both centre columns were eventually periodic, columns 0 and −1 of the usual pattern would be too, contradicting Jen.

verified_results.statement: Left barrier, corrected (Lean; part (b) of the round-1 claim refuted). Fix any driver and n ≥ 1. Left starts whose leftmost black cell is at −n correspond bijectively to the values of column −1 at steps 0..n−2 (the correspondence is triangular and permutive). So exactly 2^z edge-structured states at onset T satisfy the forced constraints on [T,2T−2], where z = #{t ∈ [T,2T−2] : c(t) = 0}. This limits only arguments that treat the onset left half as an arbitrary edge-structured state. The true onset row also carries the universal left-edge structure: D_1 ≡ 1, D_2 ≡ 0, D_3 alternating, D_4 ≡ 1, and so on, and roughly the leftmost three quarters of row T is in the settled regime. Using that structure, the word 1 is excluded from times ≤ 2T−2 alone.
verified_results.proof_outline: Light-cone and permutivity lemmas for the driven left half give existence and uniqueness by building the start one cell at a time; the count follows. The refutation of (b) is WordOneEarly: the forced constraints make the row alternate up to depth T−2, which contradicts D_2(T) = 0 when T is even and D_4(T) = 1 when T is odd.

verified_results.statement:
Period-3 forced structure (new in synthesis; computer-checked, not yet in Lean). Write phases 0, 1, 2 for the times mod 3, with c = w at those phases.
(a) w = 001. The effective boundary c ∧ σc is identically white, so from the onset the left half is the zero-boundary left half. Column −1 is black at phase 2, where c = 1. Under the driver (001)^∞, every adversarial right strip of width ≥ 12 eventually forces column 1 white at phase 0. This is smallperiods C8 (width 14), re-checked independently at width 12 with synth-lead/c8check.py. Since cell(t,−1) = c(t+1) ⊕ cell(t,1) at white times, column −1 is white at phase 0, so column −1 is eventually (0, s_k, 1). Left reconstruction then gives affine forced columns: −2 = (s_k, ¬s_k, 1); −3 = (1, 0, ¬s_{k+1}); −4 = (1, s_k⊕s_{k+1}, 0); −5 = (¬(s_k⊕s_{k+1}), s_k⊕s_{k+1}, s_{k+1}); −6 = (¬(s_k⊕s_{k+1}), s_k, ¬s_{k+2}). Nonlinearity starts at column −7.
(b) w = 011. The effective boundary is (0,1,0) and column −1 = (s_k, 0, 1). Then −2 = (s_k, 0, ¬s_{k+1}); −3 = (s_k, ¬s_{k+1}, ¬s_{k+1}); −4 = (s_k⊕¬s_{k+1}, 0, 1). Nonlinearity starts at column −5.
So two of every three values of column −1 are forced, against one of two for period 2. Exhaustive searches (smallperiods C7) find that constrained left starts of width 22 die within 32 steps, against 41 for period 2.
verified_results.proof_outline: Use the effective boundary, the identity c(t) = 1 ⇒ cell(t,−1) = ¬c(t+1), and cell(t,−1) = c(t+1) ⊕ cell(t,1) at white times. The right-strip forcing uses the adversarial reachable-set method: start from all strip states, iterate both inputs until the phase-indexed sets repeat, then read off column 1. The column formulas follow from col_{−(j+1)}(t) = col_{−j}(t+1) ⊕ (col_{−j}(t) ∨ col_{−(j−1)}(t)) with column 0 replaced by c ∧ σc; they were checked on random s by synth-lead/p3_affine.py. Scripts are in /Users/swish/.claude/jobs/b8cd2926/tmp/r30prize/synth-lead/.

most_promising_directions:
1. Period 2, the canonical first open case. Value is highest; chance of success in one round is about 2–4%. It is equivalent to c(t) = c(t+1) for infinitely many t. Attack it two-sidedly, not only through the left-only statement Q01:
- By realization, each finite right half R determines a unique left half L(R) that makes the centre alternate. Period 2 is excluded iff L(R) is never finitely supported, for every finite R.
- The right half's coherence constraints cut the per-step freedom of s from 1 bit to at most about 0.62 bits: no 00, s ∈ {01, 011, 0111, 01111}^∞, and eight forbidden pair words.
- The true onset row is far from arbitrary: roughly its leftmost three quarters is the universal settled left-diagonal structure. That is the lever that excluded the word 1 early.
- What is needed is one of: a divergent lower bound on the forced left weight; a charge that is monotone along coherent cones; or a reusable shifted clause found by zero-tail elimination. Each candidate must be tested against the stripe and the ether (infinite solutions) and against rules 15, 90, 150 and 210.
- Left-only Q01 and its barriers (no finite-state abstraction or local ranking works) are being worked on in A-* and progA-backdet.

2. Least period 4 via forced trap entry. Success would be the first full least period excluded; chance about 2–4%.
- This is the only frontier where the right half empirically always absorbs: all of more than 4000 random finite starts. Certified closed traps and Lean no-entry theorems exist, and B-edge-trap has found an ether-and-wall structure.
- What is missing is a trap-entry theorem that uses the finiteness of the true right half, because adversarial strip inputs can avoid every trap forever.
- Levers:
  - Non-adjacent Jen on far columns: if at some width every trap-avoiding input sequence is eventually periodic, entry is forced.
  - Coupling with the deterministic left half: for 0001 it is the zero-boundary left half with column −1 black every fourth step.
  - The rigid right edge.

3. Period 3 via denser left forcing. New and least explored; chance about 1–3%.
- For 001, the left half is the zero-boundary left half with column −1 eventually (0, *, 1): two of every three phases are forced, using the right-strip determination at phase 0.
- The forced columns stay affine in s through column −6. For period 2, only one phase in two is forced and the skeleton stops at column −4.
- 011 gives column −1 = (*, 0, 1), with effective boundary (0, 1, 0).
- Constrained left starts die sooner than for period 2. Whether denser forcing permits an infinite-horizon argument is unknown, and full period 3 needs both words.

4. Rigorous infinite word families and a census. Likely to succeed (about 70–80%); modest value for Problem 1 itself.
- A pumping lemma for long white runs: 0^k 1 for every k ≥ 10, and Theorem C made rigorous for all short blocks.
- Berzai's family: every word whose cyclic zero-runs all have length ≥ 19.
- Together these would give a structure theorem: every eventual period word has a black run ≤ 8 before a white cell and a white run ≤ R0.
- A Lean-checked census of all words up to length about 18, to pin down the hard core. No word of length ≤ 7 can be reached by local certificates.

5. A global mechanism using both edges. A full solution needs one; chance well under 1% per round.
- Consider time-shift defect fields d_t(p) = cell(t+P,p) ⊕ cell(t,p). Under the hypothesis, d_t(0) = 0 and d_t(−1) = ¬c(t) ∧ d_t(1).
- So left defects, which the left-edge band always seeds, can reach the centre only at white times and only paired with a right defect at column 1.
- Look for conserved or monotone quantities that rules 90, 150, 210 and 15 do not share, and test 'period-word induction' (reducing every primitive word to 0, 1 or 01).
- No candidate mechanism exists yet.

Deprioritize: these are proved dead ends or pure reformulations.
- Right absorption or strip certificates for words of length 2–7 (local obstruction).
- Left absorption: impossible by driven-left Jen.
- Finite-state abstractions or local ranking functions for Q01.
- Bounded-window or SAT horizon extensions: Condrey shows finite rows of radius w realize alternating prefixes of length about w.
- Diagonal, odometer, Mahler, ANF-degree, complexity and automaticity arguments: rules 90, 150 and 210 share them, or they are equivalent to the problem.
- Measure, entropy and randomness heuristics.
- The published 'solutions' (Das, Basta, Fradkin, Brauer, Deva, Tan).

ROLE: attack eventual period 2, the first open case, using BOTH halves and the finiteness of the configuration. Equivalent target: c(t) = c(t+1) for infinitely many t.

PROVED (Lean: staged Rule30PeriodTwo, smallperiods/lean/PeriodTwo.lean, verify-C5-rigor/).
- Normal form: c(T+2k) = 1 and c(T+2k+1) = 0 for all k. Write s_k = cell(T+2k+1,−1).
- Column −1 is black at every T+2k.
- cell(T+2k+1,1) = ¬s_k.
- s has no 00.
- cell(T+2k,−2) = cell(T+2k+1,−2) = ¬s_k.
- cell(T+2k,−3) = s_k and cell(T+2k+1,−3) = s_{k+1}.
- Column −4 is white at every T+2k+1.
- At white times, write the column-1 pairs as A = 00, B = 01, C = 11. The pair words avoid AA, BB, BC, CC, ABAB, ACBACA, CACBAC and ACACACB. Hence after its first zero, s is a concatenation of 01, 011, 0111 and 01111, i.e. zeros of column −1 are 4, 6, 8 or 10 steps apart.
- From T, the left half is the zero-boundary left half (ZBL): rule 30 on p ≤ −1 with column 0 white, started from the true row at T, which has support [−T,−1].
- Q01 ⇒ not eventually 2-periodic (Lean: not_eventually_period_two_of_Q01).
- Masked Jen ⇒ s is not eventually periodic.
- Realization: every finite right half R determines a unique left half L(R) making the centre alternate. Period 2 is excluded iff L(R) is never finitely supported, for every finite R, given that the left half at T must be the true one.
- Infinite solutions exist: the stripe …10101 is a ZBL fixed point, and B-edge-trap/ found a spatial-period-7, temporal-period-4 ether with a 0101 column. So finiteness must be used.

BARRIERS:
- No finite-state abstraction or local ranking function can prove Q01 (A-invsearch/lean/ZBLBarrier.lean, in progress).
- Finite rows of radius w realize alternating prefixes of length about w (Condrey).
- Right absorption fails for 01: for random right halves, column 1 at white times is not eventually periodic.
- The exact column-1 language at white times under (01)^∞, over all right halves, has 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 17, 25, 36, 49, 65, 88, 115, 148, 188, 237 words for n = 1..15. The per-step ratio decreases slowly (1.26 at n = 15), so whether its entropy is positive is not settled.

THIRD-PARTY (lit-oss/dl/Patto1155_rule30-foundry, text only; re-check before use):
- weak weight growth: eventually periodic s ⇒ L(R) has a 1 in every 4p-block;
- the open 'uniform deficit' conjecture 7·W_N(R) ≥ N−8, where W_N is the weight of the first N forced left cells; checked for R < 2^16 and N ≤ 256;
- the refuted 'cone-charge' bound Σ_{j≤2m} e_j ≥ ⌈m/4⌉. The weight-six integer 4329177217 passes 26 left-only latches, but its inferred right word contains 11, so it is not two-sided coherent;
- the integer form of the left half: T_b(n) = (n>>1) xor (n | (n<<1) | b), G = T_1∘T_0, with constraint G^k(n) mod 4 ∈ {1,2}.

NOTE: the true onset row is far from arbitrary. Roughly its leftmost three quarters is in the settled regime of the left diagonals (BRIEF.md: transients T_j ≈ 1.34 j), whose values are universal. verify-bbarrier/WordOneEarly.lean used exactly this (D_2 ≡ 0, D_4 ≡ 1) to exclude the word 1 early. Treat 'Q01 for true onset rows' as a weaker target that still suffices.

GOALS:
1. Exact two-sided data.
  - For every finite right half R of width ≤ 20 (more if feasible), compute the forced left half L(R) to depth ≥ 200 and its weight profile W_N.
  - For ZBL starts of width ≤ 30, compute survival under the COHERENT constraint (column −1 black at even steps AND s in the right-half-coherent language), and compare with plain Q01. Use DFS over the triangular reconstruction, as period2/ (search2.py, death_free.py, fiber2.py) and smallperiods/qsearch2.c do.
  - Decide whether the coherent column-1 language has positive entropy: compute it further with a smarter exact method.
  - For true onset rows with T ≤ 2000, record when and how the ZBL violates the constraint, and how much of row T the settled diagonals fix.
2. Search for a provable statement that forces L(R) to be infinite, or forces the ZBL from true onset rows to fail. Candidates:
  - any divergent lower bound on W_N;
  - a potential or charge that is monotone along coherent cones;
  - a shift-invariant clause found by zero-tail elimination (use SAT/z3 only to discover schemas; a final proof must be human-checkable or kernel/LRAT-checked);
  - an argument that uses the settled left-edge structure.
  Test every candidate against exhaustive small cases, the unphysical counterexample above, the stripe and the ether (a valid argument must use finite support), and the rule 15/90/150/210 controls.
3. If the full statement resists, prove the strongest new partial result you can. Examples: a two-sided strengthening of masked Jen specific to period 2; 'L(R) is infinite whenever s has an explicit property implied by coherence'.
4. Formalize in Lean whatever you prove. Start with the weak-weight-growth lemma if r2-verify has not done it.

result.honest_assessment:
Chance of fully solving Problem 1 with these methods: essentially none. It is well under 1% for round 2, and I see no path to a solution with the current toolkit.

Why:
- Every rigorous exclusion so far is one of two kinds.
  - Local: absorption and strip certificates. These provably cannot reach any word of length 2–7, so they cannot settle period 2, 3 or 4.
  - Jen-type: these need a second periodic column, which is exactly what a single periodic centre column does not provide.
- Rules 90, 150 and 210 share every structural fact we use: left-permutivity, the light cone, Jen's theorem, diagonal periodicity and the odometer structure. Yet their single-seed centre columns are eventually periodic.
- Realization shows that every eventually periodic column is produced by some infinite configuration.
- So a proof must use rule 30's OR in the chaotic interior, together with the finiteness of the seed, over an infinite time horizon.
- No mechanism that does this is known:
  - Constrained runs behave like a random-constraint model. That is strong evidence for the conjecture but is not a proof.
  - Every finite-state or local-ranking route to the period-2 statement Q01 is ruled out by the in-progress barrier results.
- Several independent efforts (rule30-foundry, placego, Berzai, cochon123) stopped at period 2, which Condrey names as the next open case.

Realistic round-2 outcomes:
- Integration and adversarial review of the 22 established results: very likely.
- New rigorous infinite families of excluded period words, plus a Lean census of the hard core: likely, about 70–80%.
- A first full period of 2 or more excluded for every transient (period 2, period 3, or least period 4): unlikely, about 5–10% combined, roughly 2–4% each.

Even that last outcome would be a publishable partial result, since period 2 is the stated next case. It would only bring Problem 1 within reach if its proof contained a genuinely new global idea that generalizes to all period words. The constant word and the word 01 are special in ways that do not obviously extend.

Calibration caveat: the shortest nonconstant word excluded so far has length 8. The third-party claims (Berzai, placego, foundry) are not yet independently verified, apart from what round 1 re-checked.
